Description: The Halloween-themed event includes spooky standards like Modest Mussorgsky’s Night on Bald Mountain (conducted by CMU Philharmonic Associate Conductor, John William Brink ) and Paul Dukas’ The Sorcerer’s Apprentice . The concert will also feature wizard of the keyboard, Tino Cardenes (current Music and Technology student of the School of Music and winner of the Philharmonic Soloist Competition, undergraduate division) performing Nikolai Kapustin’s jazzy Piano Concerto No. 2 . The heart of the program is Manuel de Falla’s magical El Amor Brujo , which includes the famous “Ritual Fire Dance.” This performance will feature recent graduate of the School of Music, mezzo-soprano Isabelle Hoyou . Kids are encouraged to come in costume and arrive early for pre-concert fun in the lobby.

Date: Monday, November 2, 2026
Venue: Posner Center
Category: Arts & Performance, Campus Life, Open to the Public
Organizer: Libraries
Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

text:

Date: Monday, November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM
Venue: Porter Hall A7F
Organizer: Civil and Environmental Engineering Department
Description: Title: Driving Measurable Value Through Owner Focused Innovation

Abstract:

Digital transformation in the built environment is increasingly defined not by technology adoption alone, but by the ability to demonstrate measurable value. AI, openBIM, VDC, digital twins, Lean practices, and performance metrics are becoming more closely connected as organizations seek better project, asset, and business outcomes.

Drawing on more than 30 years of experience in openBIM and digital innovation, including owner-focused initiatives across 30 countries, Dr. Calvin Kam will explore how governments, owners, and industry organizations can translate emerging technologies, open standards, and mandates into practical implementation strategies and measurable results.

Building on his work as Founder and CEO of Strategic Building Innovation, his work with buildingSMART International on Global openBIM Mandates and openBIM Business Value, and research associated with Stanford University’s Center for Integrated Facility Engineering (CIFE), the presentation will examine how frameworks such as the VDC Scorecard can help organizations connect information requirements, quality controls, technology adoption, KPIs, and performance with broader business value.

Looking forward, the session will explore how AI, openBIM, and VDC can increasingly enable digital twins, GIS, IoT, sustainability, and decarbonization - creating a stronger foundation for informed decision-making, smarter mandates, and improved w

Bio: Praneeth Vepakomma is currently a Visiting Assistant Professor at MIT in IDSS and is an Assistant Professor at MBZUAI. He previously obtained his PhD at MIT in and works on trustworthy/responsible computation that includes a sub-focus on distributed (resource-efficient) and private computation in statistics, ML and data science at large. He has extensive industrial experience across Meta, Apple, Amazon, Motorola Solutions, Corning and several startups. His research focuses on developing algorithms for distributed computation in statistics & machine learning under constraints of privacy, & efficiency.

He won the Meta PhD research fellowship in Applied Statistics, two SERC Scholarships (for Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing) from MIT’s Schwarzman college of computing. He co-founded a research based non-profit (Integrity Distributed) that won the Financial Times Digital Innovation Award. He won a Best Student Paper Award at FL-IJCAI, a Baidu Best Paper Award at NeurIPS-SpicyFL and a Best Paper Runner Up Award at FG-2021. His technical work is inspired by foundations of non-asymptotic statistics, randomized algorithms, learning augmented algorithms, combinatorics, and at times just by systems design. text:

Event: Kearra Amaya Gopee: Visiting Artist Lecture
Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 at 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM
Venue: Carnegie Museum of Art
Category: Conferences, Panels & Lectures, Open to the Public
Organizer: School of Art
Description: Join us for an evening with artist Kearra Amaya Gopee as they share an in-depth look at their practice and the works featured in If the word we: 59th Carnegie International. Lectures are free and open to the public.

About the Artist

Kearra Amaya Gopee (born 1994, Miami, FL, raised in Carapichaima, Kairi (Trinidad and Tobago); lives on Lenape land in New York) is an anti-disciplinary artist and facilitator. Using video, sculpture, sound, and writing, they identify both violence and time as primary conditions that undergird the anti-Black world in which they work. Gopee has shown work at documenta 15, Kassel, Germany (2022), and The Kitchen, among other international film venues. They have participated in residencies at Skowhegan, the International Studio and Curatorial Program, Headlands Center for the Arts, and NLS Kingston. They have been awarded fellowships at MacDowell, the Leslie Lohman Museum, Queer|Art, and the Global Fund for Women. In 2024, Gopee was an Elaine G. Weitzen Fellow at the Whitney Museum Independent Study Program. They have lectured at Emory University, Rutgers University, and the Caltech-Huntington Program in Visual Culture. In 2025, Gopee was an artist in residence at MASS MoCA. They hold an MFA from University of California, Los Angeles, with a concentration in interdisciplinary studio and a BFA in photography and imaging from New York University.

Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Brett Helsel Career Development Professor in Computer Science & Engineering
University of Washington

Talk Title: Talk title coming soon

Bio: Franziska Roesner is a professor in the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, where her research focuses on computer security and privacy. Her interests are broad within that domain, identifying and addressing security and privacy challenges faced by end users of existing and emerging technologies. Roesner co-directs the Security and Privacy Research Lab.

She is also an adjunct professor in the Information School, the Electrical & Computer Engineering Department and the Human Centered Design and Engineering Department at the University of Washington. In addition, she is affiliated with the UW Tech Policy Lab and the UW Center for an Informed Public.

Roesner is chair of the USENIX Security steering committee (after co-chairing the conference in 2020) and was on the USENIX Enigma steering committee (after co-chairing that conference in 2018 and 2019).

She is the recipient of an NSF CAREER Award (2017), an Emerging Leader Alumni Award from the UT Austin College of Natural Sciences (2017), an MIT Technology Review Innovators Under 35 Award (2017), a Google Security and Privacy Research Award (2017), an Undergraduate Research Mentor Award (2020), a Consumer Reports Digital Lab Fellowship (2021), and a Google Research Scholar Award (2022).

title: EPP Seminar: Sonia Mangones — Transportation, Air Pollution, and Inequalities: Evidence from Bogotá, Colombia (Monday, November 9, 2026)
text:
EPP Seminar: Sonia Mangones — Transportation, Air Pollution, and Inequalities: Evidence from Bogotá, Colombia takes place on Monday, November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM at Wean Hall 4110.
Event: EPP Seminar: Sonia Mangones — Transportation, Air Pollution, and Inequalities: Evidence from Bogotá, Colombia
Date: Monday, November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM
Venue: Wean Hall 4110
Organizer: Engineering and Public Policy Department
Description: Environmental justice research often examines the burden of pollution in relation to the population’s socioeconomic vulnerability. Climate justice research examines differential responsibility, asking who emits and who ultimately carries the burden they create. Urban mobility justice research rarely combines these two questions empirically, even though mobility is where they intersect most directly, since travel generates emissions and also shapes where resulting pollution concentrations fall across the city. This talk presents findings from an empirical study of Bogotá, Colombia, that measures both sides of this relationship at the level of city blocks, combining residential pollution concentration (NO2 and PM2.5) with a block-level proxy for travel-emission responsibility built from official mobility and emissions data. Two findings challenge a simple story in which the poor pollute least and suffer most. First, pollution concentration does not increase monotonically with deprivation; it peaks at intermediate socioeconomic levels. Second, emission responsibility does decline cleanly with vulnerability, but the resulting imbalance, where responsibility is low and pollution concentration is high, concentrates in population segments that can only be identified by combining policy instruments that separately inform socioeconomic vulnerability and the spatial distribution of the imbalance. Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

title: Departmental Seminar: Dr. Iain Cheeseman (Wednesday, November 11, 2026)
text:
Departmental Seminar: Dr. Iain Cheeseman takes place on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at 12:30 PM at Mellon Institute (MCS), 348 Conference Room.
Event: Departmental Seminar: Dr. Iain Cheeseman
Date: Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at 12:30 PM to 1:40 PM
Venue: Mellon Institute (MCS), 348 Conference Room
Organizer: Biological Sciences Department
Description: Guest Speaker: Iain Cheeseman, PhD

Professor of Biology at MIT

Core Member, Whitehead Institute

Title: TBA

Our lab is fascinated by the molecular machinery that directs core cellular processes, and in particular how these processes are modulated and rewired across different physiological contexts. Our work has focused on the proteins that direct chromosome segregation and cell division, including the macromolecular kinetochore structure that mediates chromosome-microtubule interactions. Although cell division is an essential cellular process, this machinery is remarkably flexible in its composition and properties, which can vary dramatically between species and are even modulated within the same organism — over the cell cycle, during development, and across diverse physiological situations. To define the basis by which the kinetochore and other core cellular structures are rewired to adapt to diverse situations and functional requirements, we are currently investigating diverse transcriptional, translational, and post-translational mechanisms that act to generate proteomic variability both within individual cells and across tissues, cell state, development, and disease.

Category: Conferences, Panels & Lectures
Organizer: Languages, Cultures & Applied Linguistics Department
Description: Translingual Borders: Refugee Testimony and the Politics of Translation

Isabelle Chen , assistant professor of global French studies, will challenge the assumption that translation is a liberatory practice — one that enables people to cross linguistic, cultural and geographic borders — by examining how translation can also reinforce borders, reproduce unequal power dynamics and constrain individual agency.

Focusing on Shumona Sinha’s novel Assommons les pauvres ! ( Down with the Poor! ), Dr. Chen’s talk explores the experiences of a Bengali interpreter working with asylum seekers in France. She examines how Sinha uses translation both as a literary strategy and a central thematic motif to portray interpretation as a potential barrier to human mobility and freedom.

Drawing on translation theory and recent migration data, Dr. Chen considers what literary representations of translation can reveal about its real-world consequences — and about the roles of multilingualism, interpretation and language in immigration policy and advocacy today.

text:
ACO Seminar: Veit Elser (Cornell University) takes place on Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 3:00 PM at Wean Hall 8220.
Event: ACO Seminar: Veit Elser (Cornell University)
Date: Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM
Venue: Wean Hall 8220
Category: Conferences, Panels & Lectures, Open to the Public
Organizer: Mathematical Sciences Department
Description: Speaker: Veit Elser , Cornell University

A greedy method for solving even hard problems

Abstract: Greed is a great instinct for solving problems. Its geometrical analog is a projection. Say your problem has many variables. It’s always possible to let them live in a continuous space, and define solutions to your problem as some subset in that space. A projection is the greedy operation of moving an arbitrary point to the set as efficiently as possible — by the least Euclidean distance. For many kinds of sets, even discrete and other highly non-convex ones, the projection computations are easy. Of course we know that cannot be the case when the task at hand is truly hard. Fortunately, even hard problems can be formulated as finding a point in the intersection of two sets, where projecting to each set individually is easy. This talk describes a general method that uses two easy projections, iteratively, to solve hard problems. After some history I will go over several examples, including sudoku, square packing, and data clustering. Problem requests will be considered if received (at ve10@cornell.edu) at least one week before the talk.

Description: The City-Women

Join Café con Libros for a conversation celebrating the release of The City-Women , the debut play by playwright, actor, and musician Mallorie Sievert .

Set in a 17th-century cloistered convent in Latin America, The City-Women is a sapphic historical romance that follows four Latine women navigating faith, identity, and love within a strict religious environment. Mallorie will be joined by director, playwright, and longtime collaborator Sara LiBrandi for a discussion exploring the intersections of feminism, queerness, Christianity, and Latinidad, followed by an audience Q&A and book signing.

About the Author

Mallorie Sievert (she/her) is a Latina playwright, actor, and musician based in New York City. She graduated from Elon University in 2024, and The City-Women is her debut play. Her acting credits include Shucked (Broadway First National Tour) and Heartbreak Hotel (Engeman Theater).

title: Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections (Saturday, November 14, 2026)
text:
Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections takes place on Saturday, November 14, 2026 at Posner Center.
Event: Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections
Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026
Venue: Posner Center
Category: Arts & Performance, Campus Life, Open to the Public
Organizer: Libraries
Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Exhibit Hours

During the summer, the Posner Center operates by appointment only . Contact Sam Lemley to make an appointment to visit the exhibit.

title: Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress (Monday, November 16, 2026)
text:
Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress takes place on Monday, November 16, 2026 at 9:30 AM at CUC – Danforth Conference Room.
Event: Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress
Date: Monday, November 16, 2026 at 9:30 AM to 11:00 AM
Venue: CUC – Danforth Conference Room
Category: Career & Professional Development, Health & Wellness, Training & Workshops
Organizer: Office of the Vice Provost for Faculty
Description: This faculty-designed professional development opportunity serves as a broad overview of how best to aid students at Carnegie Mellon University.

This session combines 30 minutes of asynchronous work in FocusU with a 90-minute, in-person presentation. Upon completing the training, faculty should be able to (1) articulate key findings about the CMU student mental health experience, (2) describe the vital role of faculty in supporting students, (3) identify the appropriate methods to assist students, and (4) describe the available support resources on campus.

Please note that this training is one of three options that faculty can complete to fulfill required training on student mental health and well-being. As part of CMU’s ongoing commitment to student mental health and well-being, all faculty members are expected to complete professional development focused on recognizing and supporting students in distress. Faculty may choose from the three training options listed on the Counseling & Psychological Services website (https://www.cmu.edu/counseling/services/cope.html#trainings). For more information, please refer to Provost Garrett and Dean Casalegno’s message to faculty (https://www.cmu.edu/leadership/the-provost/campus-comms/11-05-25).

Bio: Adam Smith is a Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at Boston University. His research interests lie in data privacy and cryptography, and their connections to machine learning, statistics, information theory, and quantum computing. He obtained his Ph.D. from MIT in 2004 and has held visiting positions at the Weizmann Institute of Science, UCLA, and Harvard. He previously was a Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at Penn State. He received a Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE) in 2009; a 2016 Theory of Cryptography Test of Time award; the 2019 Eurocrypt Test of Time award; and the 2017 Gödel Prize.

Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
Venue: Posner Center
Category: Arts & Performance, Campus Life, Open to the Public
Organizer: Libraries
Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Description: Co-creating tomorrow: Community Driven Engineering for a Resilient Future” is a webinar series exploring the critical intersection of community wisdom and engineering expertise in the face of a changing climate. title: Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections (Friday, November 20, 2026)
text:
Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections takes place on Friday, November 20, 2026 at Posner Center.
Event: Rare Books & Ancestral Machines: The Inaugural Exhibition of the Posner Center for Special Collections
Date: Friday, November 20, 2026
Venue: Posner Center
Category: Arts & Performance, Campus Life, Open to the Public
Organizer: Libraries
Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Exhibit Hours

During the summer, the Posner Center operates by appointment only . Contact Sam Lemley to make an appointment to visit the exhibit.

Monday, closed

Organizer: CyLab
Description: Speaker: Andrew Ilyas
Assistant Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering & Software and Societal Systems
Carnegie Mellon University

Talk Title: Talk title coming soon

Abstract: Abstract coming soon

Bio:

Andrew Ilyas is an assistant professor at CMU. Previously, he was a Stein Fellow at Stanford Statistics and a Ph.D. student MIT, where he was fortunate to be advised by Costis DaskalakisOpens in new window and Aleksander MadryOpens in new window and supported by an Open Philanthropy AI FellowshipOpens in new window. Ilyas attended MIT for undergrad, majoring in CS and in Math. Outside of research, I enjoy playing soccer and table tennis.

Ilyas’s goal is to uncover general principles that describe and predict the behavior of ML systems—ideally enabling predictably reliable future systems. This goal entails combining statistical tools with large-scale experiments to precisely understand the ML “pipeline,” from training data (and the way we collect it), to learning algorithms, to deployment. He also likes thinking broadly about (human) trust in AI systems.

Venue: Mellon Institute (MCS), 348 Conference Room
Organizer: Biological Sciences Department
Description: Guest Speaker: Joshua Weinstein, PhD

Assistant Professor of Medicine

University of Chicago

Title: TBA

Joshua Weinstein is a biophysicist and molecular technologist. He works on developing DNA-based technologies for high-throughput encoding and decoding of biological information with a view toward applications in biology and medicine. He has previously worked on applying massively parallel DNA sequencing to the study of immune receptor repertoires. Recently, he invented DNA microscopy, an imaging modality that uses DNA rather than light as an imaging medium in order to generate detailed pictures of how genetic diversity distributes spatially across biological specimens.

Departmental Host: Professor Kaplow

Date: Thursday, December 3, 2026
Venue: Posner Center
Category: Arts & Performance, Campus Life, Open to the Public
Organizer: Libraries
Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Description: This faculty-designed professional development opportunity serves as a broad overview of how best to aid students at Carnegie Mellon University.

This session combines 30 minutes of asynchronous work in FocusU with a 90-minute, in-person presentation. Upon completing the training, faculty should be able to (1) articulate key findings about the CMU student mental health experience, (2) describe the vital role of faculty in supporting students, (3) identify the appropriate methods to assist students, and (4) describe the available support resources on campus.

Please note that this training is one of three options that faculty can complete to fulfill required training on student mental health and well-being. Faculty may choose from the three training options listed on the Counseling & Psychological Services website (https://www.cmu.edu/counseling/services/cope.html#trainings). text:
CERCA Webinar with Orange Country Water District takes place on Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 3:30 PM at Virtual - Register Below.
Event: CERCA Webinar with Orange Country Water District
Date: Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM
Venue: Virtual - Register Below
Organizer: Civil and Environmental Engineering Department
Description: “Co-creating tomorrow: Community Driven Engineering for a Resilient Future” is a webinar series exploring the critical intersection of community wisdom and engineering expertise in the face of a changing climate. Organized by CERCA, CMU CEE’s Center for Engineering Resilience and Climate Adaptation, this series will foster a deeper understanding of how community engagement can enhance the effectiveness, equity, and sustainability of climate adaptation initiatives.

The Orange County Water District (OCWD) manages the Orange County Groundwater Basin, which provides approximately 85% of the water supply for 2.5 million people. Maintaining a reliable groundwater supply in a highly urbanized coastal basin requires an integrated approach that includes seawater intrusion protection, water reuse, stormwater capture, and managed aquifer recharge (MAR).

Seawater intrusion has been a challenge in the Orange County Groundwater Basin since the 1920s. In response, OCWD constructed the Talbert Seawater Intrusion Barrier in the 1970s, creating a hydraulic barrier to protect the basin from further seawater intrusion. Today, OCWD continues to operate and improve its coastal barriers and is evaluating development of a new barrier in the Sunset Gap to address an additional potential pathway for seawater intrusion. Bill Leever, OCWD Principal Hydrogeologist, will discuss the history, operation, and future of OCWD’s seawater intrusion barrier program.

title: Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress (Friday, December 11, 2026)
text:
Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress takes place on Friday, December 11, 2026 at 10:00 AM at CUC – Danforth Conference Room.
Event: Supporting Student Well-Being: Faculty Professional Development in Recognizing and Assisting Students in Distress
Date: Friday, December 11, 2026 at 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM
Venue: CUC – Danforth Conference Room
Category: Career & Professional Development, Health & Wellness, Training & Workshops
Organizer: Office of the Vice Provost for Faculty
Description: This faculty-designed professional development opportunity serves as a broad overview of how best to aid students at Carnegie Mellon University.

This session combines 30 minutes of asynchronous work in FocusU with a 90-minute, in-person presentation. Upon completing the training, faculty should be able to (1) articulate key findings about the CMU student mental health experience, (2) describe the vital role of faculty in supporting students, (3) identify the appropriate methods to assist students, and (4) describe the available support resources on campus.

Please note that this training is one of three options that faculty can complete to fulfill required training on student mental health and well-being. As part of CMU’s ongoing commitment to student mental health and well-being, all faculty members are expected to complete professional development focused on recognizing and supporting students in distress. Faculty may choose from the three training options listed on the Counseling & Psychological Services website (https://www.cmu.edu/counseling/services/cope.html#trainings). For more information, please refer to Provost Garrett and Dean Casalegno’s message to faculty (https://www.cmu.edu/leadership/the-provost/campus-comms/11-05-25).

Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

Event: Kwanzaa Begins
Date: Saturday, December 26, 2026
Organizer: Inclusive Holiday Observations and Interfaith Calendar
Description: An African-American and Pan-African holiday celebrating family, community, and culture, Kwanzaa is a secular observance with some religious participation. Each day of Kwanzaa celebrates one of the Nguzo Saba, or the seven life principle in the language, Kiswahili. They are honored with candle-lighting each day of the season: umoja (unity), kujichagulia (self-determination), ujima (collective work and responsibility), ujamaa (cooperative economics), nia (purpose), kuumba (creativity), and imani (faith). Symbols include crops. Kwanzaa ends on January 1.

Description: The Posner Center is a cabinet of rarities and technological marvels: paper-and-string cipher machines, centuries-old books, cogwheel computers and 19th century “digital” images. Part museum and part laboratory, it is a site for discovery, research, and innovation with the materials of the past.

Rare Books & Ancestral Machines features more than 30 books and objects from the Posner Center’s holdings. Many of these materials are on view for the first time. The exhibition inaugurates the newly renovated Center, surveying its collections and tracing more than four centuries of scientific inquiry and learning. Organized into five thematic sections — mechanical computing, robotics, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and scholarly method — the exhibit explores the histories of these disciplines, uncovering abandoned prototypes and long-forgotten technologies.

What will you discover?

Description: Watch Night or Freedom’s Eve is celebrated in many African American or Black Christian Churches. It celebrates and commemorates the Emancipation Proclamation (enacted January 1, 1863) which freed American slaves during the American Civil War. Watch night worship services are now annual New Year’s Eve traditions, recalling faith, freedom, strength, and community. It is celebrated on the evening of December 31.

title: Kwanzaa Ends (Friday, January 1, 2027)
text:
Kwanzaa Ends takes place on Friday, January 1, 2027.
Event: Kwanzaa Ends
Date: Friday, January 1, 2027
Organizer: Inclusive Holiday Observations and Interfaith Calendar
Description: An African-American and Pan-African holiday celebrating family, community, and culture, Kwanzaa is a secular observance with some religious participation. Each day of Kwanzaa celebrates one of the Nguzo Saba, or the seven life principle in the language, Kiswahili. They are honored with candle-lighting each day of the season: umoja (unity), kujichagulia (self-determination), ujima (collective work and responsibility), ujamaa (cooperative economics), nia (purpose), kuumba (creativity), and imani (faith). Symbols include crops. Kwanzaa began on December 26.

text:
Jonathan González: Visiting Artist Lecture takes place on Tuesday, January 26, 2027 at 5:30 PM at College of Fine Arts.
Event: Jonathan González: Visiting Artist Lecture
Date: Tuesday, January 26, 2027 at 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM
Venue: College of Fine Arts
Category: Conferences, Panels & Lectures, Open to the Public
Organizer: School of Art
Description: Join us for an evening with artist Jonathan González as they share an in-depth look at their practice and the work featured in If the word we: 59th Carnegie International. Lectures are free and open to the public.

The Strikebreakers

The Strikebreakers is a new site-specific, four-hour performance conceived for the Grand Staircase of Carnegie Museum of Art. Performed by five dancers over five consecutive days, the work unfolds as a slow transformation of bodies, relationships, and collective attention, using the museum’s architecture as both stage and collaborator.

Drawing its title from the complicated history of labor, industry, and Western Pennsylvania, The Strikebreakers does not seek to reenact a historical event. Instead, it approaches the figure of the worker as a choreographic proposition: a body shaped by repetition, endurance, care, fatigue, solidarity, and the continual negotiation between individual agency and collective responsibility. Historical archives surrounding labor movements and Black social life circulate throughout the work not as illustrations, but as conditions that quietly inform its movement, rhythm, and atmosphere.

The performance is less concerned with representing history than with asking how history continues to move through bodies in the present. Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Then there was the sound of unrest and protest. Things went silent again, and then there was

Description: Piano Lumière: Halloween
Join pianists Jimmy Liu and Kevin Lee Sun for Piano Lumière: Halloween , a two-piano concert presented in an intimate setting surrounded by thousands of glowing candles at Duquesne University's PNC Recital Hall.
This program features music written for two pianos, including Rachmaninoff's electrifying Tarantella , Saint-Saëns' evocative Danse Macabre , Bach's famously recognizable Toccata , Liszt's Totentanz in a rare version for three pianos, and more. The program will also spotlight the talents of youth pianist Thomas Ngan, Duquesne faculty member Nathália Kato Giordano, and Duquesne student Zoey Wolfe.
Set against a luminous autumn atmosphere, Piano Lumière offers an evening of compelling music, from beloved favorites to virtuosic masterworks.

text:
Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. title: Piano Lumière: Halloween (Sunday, October 18, 2026)
text:
Piano Lumière: Halloween takes place on Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 3:00 PM at Duquesne University.
Event: Piano Lumière: Halloween
Date: Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 3:00 PM to 4:15 PM
Recurs: On 2 selected dates
Venue: Duquesne University, 600 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15282
Category: Family
Organizer: Presto Piano Studio LLC
Description: Piano Lumière: Halloween
Join pianists Jimmy Liu and Kevin Lee Sun for Piano Lumière: Halloween , a two-piano concert presented in an intimate setting surrounded by thousands of glowing candles at Duquesne University's PNC Recital Hall.
This program features music written for two pianos, including Rachmaninoff's electrifying Tarantella , Saint-Saëns' evocative Danse Macabre , Bach's famously recognizable Toccata , Liszt's Totentanz in a rare version for three pianos, and more. The program will also spotlight the talents of youth pianist Thomas Ngan, Duquesne faculty member Nathália Kato Giordano, and Duquesne student Zoey Wolfe.
Set against a luminous autumn atmosphere, Piano Lumière offers an evening of compelling music, from beloved favorites to virtuosic masterworks.

Sunday, October 18, 2026 – 3:00 PM

Description: Step onto the 50-yard line for the New Hazlett’s first-ever co-production with DEMASKUS Theater Collective: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy . Written by Franky D. When Imani Othello is named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise, the pressure mounts on and off the field. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. text:

Date: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 7:30 PM to 9:30 PM
Venue: Pittsburgh Public Theater, 621 Penn Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Category: arts
Organizer: The Public Theater & Fiasco Theater
Price: 99
Description: Fiasco Theater and The Public partner to celebrate a hidden American classic: THE VERGE by Susan Glaspell, Pulitzer Prize winner and founder of the Provincetown Players. In Glaspell’s 1921 masterpiece, botanist Claire Archer is on a quest to create a new life: a plant unlike any that has ever come before. When her husband, lover, and soulmate each arrive in her greenhouse seeking heat in a snowstorm, chaos ensues. But as Claire pushes–sometimes violently—against the constraints of her own good breeding, she wonders if the only way to transcend boundaries is to destroy them. By turns witty farce, devastating philosophical debate, and scathing feminist cry, THE VERGE defies genre and pierces the bounds of theatrical realism. Jessie Austrian directs this new Fiasco production, featuring Tony Award winner Miriam Silverman.

Description: With a legendary career spanning more than five decades, KANSAS has firmly established itself as one of the most iconic bands in classic rock history. Since emerging from Topeka, Kansas, and releasing its self-titled debut album in 1974, the band has sold more than 30 million albums worldwide.

KANSAS has released 16 studio albums and five live albums, earning eight gold albums, three sextuple-platinum albums, a platinum live album, and multi-platinum singles including the classic rock staples "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind." The band's music dominated the charts throughout the 1970s and 1980s, with KANSAS appearing on the Billboard charts for more than 200 weeks and performing to sold-out arenas across North America, Europe, and Japan.

Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. title: Ami Taf Ra & Kamasi Washington presenting The Prophet & The Madman (Friday, November 6, 2026)
text:

Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 at 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM
Venue: City Winery Pittsburgh, 1627 Smallman St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Category: drink
Organizer: City Winery Pittsburgh
Description: Ami Taf Ra brings her sweeping, cross cultural sound to City Winery Pittsburgh this November, joined by acclaimed saxophonist, composer, and producer K amasi Washington for a tour presentation of her debut album, The Prophet and the Madman. Produced by Washington and released on Brainfeeder, the album draws on Moroccan Gnawa, Arabic musical tradition, gospel, soul, and spiritual jazz, inspired in part by Kahlil Gibran's writing on healing and ancestral memory. Ami's commanding, operatic voice carries the record from intimacy to theatrical release.
The partnership between Ami and Washington anchors the project, heard most clearly on "How I Became a Madman," a meditation on the tension between chaos and clarity. Together they build something that feels both rooted in tradition and pointed toward what comes next, connecting North African and Middle Eastern music with the improvisational spirit of contemporary jazz.
Ami's international resume includes performances across Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and the United States, among them the Dutch Royal Metropole Orchestra, the Hollywood Bowl Jazz Festival, and City Winery Boston. Washington, a Grammy winner and Emmy nominee, remains one of his generation's defining musical voices, moving fluently between jazz, soul, hip hop, classical, and screen work.

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. text:

Category: arts
Organizer: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre
Description: Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre (PBT)’s Pointe in Time fundraiser is a top 10 annual event that brings over 400 arts patrons together in support of PBT’s mainstage programming, arts education in schools and community centers, classes for individuals with disabilities, and funding for its Bridge Scholarship program. Scholarships cover all tuition costs (school year and summer) as well as associated costs (pointe shoes, leotards and tights) which can cost up to $70,000 per student.
For 57 years, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre has inspired our community and made it a more beautiful place – on the stage, in the studio and in our neighborhoods. Join us in celebrating PBT’s Season of Wonder!
The evening includes a multi-course dining experience for guests as they enjoy exclusive world-premiere performances by PBT company artists and PBT School students. A silent and live auction, pointe shoe raffle, and dancing are all a part of the night’s festivities.
We invite you to gather family, friends, colleagues and clients, and join us for an unforgettable night celebrating PBT’s world-class art and life-changing programs.

title: I Will Belong To Only Me (Sunday, November 22, 2026)
text:
I Will Belong To Only Me runs from Sunday, November 22, 2026 to Friday, April 30, 2027 at August Wilson African American Cultural Center.
Event: I Will Belong To Only Me
Date: Sunday, November 22, 2026 at 3:00 PM to Friday, April 30, 2027 at 5:00 PM
Recurs: Runs Nov 22 – Apr 30 (160 days)
Venue: August Wilson African American Cultural Center, 980 Liberty Ave Pittsburgh, PA 15222
Organizer: AWAACC
Description: PEJU ALATISE: I WILL BELONG TO ONLY ME | weekdays 3pm-6pm, weekends 1pm-5pm Exhibition dates are available one month in advance with online sales closing 2 hours before the galleries open each day. Tickets can be purchased on site as a walk-in for same day or future dates. Titled after a line from her own writing, I Will Belong to Only Me marks the first U.S. solo survey of Peju Alatise (b. 1975 in Lagos, Nigeria). A defining figure in contemporary African art, this exhibition brings together two decades of her work across sculpture, installation, text, and film. Anchored by her celebrated installation Flying Girls (2015–16), I Will Belong to Only Me embodies Alatise’s artistic prowess, conceptual depth, and multidisciplinary command across architecture, painting, sculpture, and storytelling. Merging Yorùbá cosmology with poetic form, Alatise builds spaces where imagination is resistance and African girlhood is centered, protected, and celebrated. ABOUT THE ARTIST Peju Alatise (b. 1975, Lagos) is a Nigerian interdisciplinary artist, architect, and author whose practice spans sculpture, installation, painting, film, and fiction. She lives and works between Lagos, Nigeria and Glasgow, UK. Trained in architecture at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Alatise began her career balancing architectural work with studio practice. Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Then there was the sound of unrest and protest. Things went silent again, and then there was

text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Sunday, December 13, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. title: Aaron Lewis (Thursday, December 17, 2026)
text:
Aaron Lewis takes place on Thursday, December 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM at Event Center.
Event: Aaron Lewis
Date: Thursday, December 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM
Venue: Event Center, Cincinnati, OH
Organizer: Hard Rock Casino Cincinnati
Description: Aaron Lewis, the Vermont-born powerhouse first found success with Staind - the 2000s-era hard rockers who injected meditative muscle into an era better known for mindless aggression. But while that band is still very much alive, it was never enough to satisfy Lewis’ creative drive. Embracing his roots to earn a rare second round of success, a series of solo Country projects have led to two No. 1 Billboard Country Album debuts - TOWN LINE (2011) and SINNER (2016) - plus a PLATINUM collab with heroes George Jones and Charlie Daniels (“Country Boy”), and a GOLD-certified Billboard No. 1 with “Am I The Only One” in 2021. Lewis’ 2022 solo album followed suit, with FRAYED AT BOTH ENDS emerging as the best-selling Country album in America but he never wrote songs for the stats. No matter the sonic setting, Lewis writes and sings to get his truth out and his latest album THE HILL (2024) is no different.

Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Friday, December 25, 2026 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Friday, December 25, 2026 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. title: August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC (Friday, January 1, 2027)
text:
August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC takes place on Friday, January 1, 2027 at August Wilson African American Cultural Center.
Event: August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape - AWAACC
Date: Friday, January 1, 2027 to 11:59 PM
Venue: August Wilson African American Cultural Center, 980 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: August Wilson African American Cultural Center
Description: "August Wilson: The Writer’s Landscape" is the first-ever permanent exhibition dedicated to Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright August Wilson, exploring how his Pittsburgh upbringing profoundly shaped his acclaimed American Century Cycle. This 3,600-square-foot exhibit guides visitors through three acts: "The Coffee Shop," inspired by his early observational writing, a replica of "The Office" showcasing his personal items and manuscripts, and "The Street," a recreation of Pittsburgh’s Hill District featuring an interactive map, video, and authentic props and costumes from his Broadway productions. Attendees will gain insight into major themes from his plays and discover the timeless relevance of his artistic legacy.

Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Then there was the sound of unrest and protest. Things went silent again, and then there was

Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. title: Hprizm: Sound of the City (Sunday, January 24, 2027)
text:

Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Sunday, January 24, 2027 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Hprizm: Sound of the City takes place on Saturday, January 30, 2027 at 11:00 AM at Wood Street Galleries.
Event: Hprizm: Sound of the City
Date: Saturday, January 30, 2027 at 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Recurs: Every Wed – Sun, weekly
Venue: Wood Street Galleries, 601 Wood St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Description: Sound of the City is an immersive audio installation and listening environment by NYC born artist and composer Hprizm, whose practice spans a wide array of genres, including music, performance and multimedia installations. He is a co-founder of the seminal hip-hop group Antipop Consortium, an experimental collective known for their lyrical approach to electronic music.
Centered on a sonic score that moves between abstract noise and melodic interludes, Sound of the City collapses vinyl records, tape loops and granular synthesis with audio footage captured by Hprizm over the past few years. Wielding his phone as a primary recording device, the artist took notice of his sonic environment while traversing New York City and western Pennsylvania, where he partially resides. In his own words, “The sound of the city, in a literal sense, is dense. Buried histories rumble beneath the foundation of brick. Crate digging and knowledge of self unearthed a cultural medium that informs my process.”
For Hprizm, sound carries strong implications—not only about personal narrative, but about socioeconomic conditions and resources as well. He writes, “Within the throughline for most of my work is an interrelation between memory and sonic imprints. Over the course of the last few years, with global events in mind, I noticed how much the sonic landscape changed. During the pandemic, the streets were quiet. Description: Support emerging talent and join us for Beta Stage, a monthly showcase of fresh comedy! Experience the excitement of being a part of the creative process as we provide a platform for producers to present and refine new ideas in front of a live audience. This monthly showcase is the place to see tomorrow’s comedy today!

title: 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering (Monday, April 19, 2027)
text:
3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering runs from Monday, April 19, 2027 to Tuesday, April 20, 2027 at Milton Hall.
Event: 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering
Date: Monday, April 19, 2027 at 9:30 AM to Tuesday, April 20, 2027 at 6:30 PM
Recurs: Runs Apr 19 – Apr 20 (2 days)
Venue: Milton Hall, Ridge Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15212, USA
Organizer: PAGES
Description: Following the success of our previous conferences, we are delighted to announce the 3rd International Conference on Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine & Tissue Engineering (STEMCELL-2027), which will take place on April 19–20, 2027 in Milan, Italy. STEMCELL-2027 aims to bring together leading scientists, researchers, clinicians, academicians, and industry professionals from around the world to share knowledge, discuss emerging research, and promote global collaborations in the rapidly advancing fields of stem cell science and regenerative medicine. The conference will highlight the latest developments in stem cell biology, regenerative therapies, tissue engineering, cellular technologies, and clinical applications. Participants will gain valuable insights into innovative research, technological advancements, and future directions shaping modern biomedical science. The scientific program will feature keynote lectures, plenary sessions, oral and poster presentations, and networking opportunities, providing an excellent platform for participants to exchange ideas, present their research, and build international partnerships. We warmly invite researchers, healthcare professionals, industry experts, and students to join us in Milan, Italy, for STEMCELL-2027 and contribute to advancing the future of regenerative medicine and global healthcare.
Best Regards, R Gayathri | Conference Secretary

title: GALLIM (Saturday, April 24, 2027)
text:
GALLIM takes place on Saturday, April 24, 2027 at Byham Theater.
Event: GALLIM
Date: Saturday, April 24, 2027
Venue: Byham Theater, 101 6th St, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Dance Council
Description: The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust presents a vibrant calendar of ballet and dance performances, alongside diverse visual arts exhibitions. Attendees can experience a wide range of dance, from cultural experiences like TAARi The African Experience and contemporary works by A.I.M. by Kyle Abraham, to classical ballets such as *A Midsummer Night's Dream* and *The Nutcracker* (including a sensory-friendly option), alongside celebrity shows like Derek Hough's *Symphony of Dance*. Complementing the stage, galleries showcase compelling exhibitions on topics ranging from Frank Lloyd Wright's regional impact and Michael Zagaris's NFL photography to contemporary art by Sharmistha Ray and a Juried Visual Arts Exhibition. This curated schedule offers enriching cultural experiences for diverse audiences across various venues.

title: Shikeith, Hold (Thursday, April 29, 2027)
text:
Shikeith, Hold runs from Thursday, April 29, 2027 to Wednesday, June 30, 2027 at Arts Landing.
Event: Shikeith, Hold
Date: Thursday, April 29, 2027 to Wednesday, June 30, 2027
Recurs: Runs Apr 29 – Jun 30 (63 days)
Venue: Arts Landing, 805 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: Pittsburgh Cultural Trust
Price: 0
Description: Installed at Arts Landing, Hold is made of weathering steel and neon. The sculpture extends Project Blue Space, Shikeith’s initiative exploring the spiritual, cultural, and political relationships Black communities have forged with water. Its title gestures toward both the hold of a slave ship and the body as a vessel of memory, feeling, and endurance. Within, the work glows haint blue, a color rooted in Gullah Geechee traditions of protection. Its light pulses like breath. Over time, the steel exterior will deepen and shift with weather. About the Artist Shikeith is a visual artist and filmmaker whose work explores psychological landscapes and how history persists in the present. Hold, his first public art commission, brings this inquiry into civic space. Hold by Shikeith is commissioned by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust for Arts Landing. Hold is developed as part of Project Blue Space, a web-based platform mapping the cultural, spiritual, and political relationships Black communities have forged with water. The project is funded by the Mellon Foundation’s Humanities in Place initiative.

Organizer: Arcade Comedy Theater
Description: Support emerging talent and join us for Beta Stage, a monthly showcase of fresh comedy! Experience the excitement of being a part of the creative process as we provide a platform for producers to present and refine new ideas in front of a live audience. New concepts get the opportunity to be workshopped live, allowing for real-time feedback and audience interaction. This show is a part of Arcade’s incubator series, which is all about experimentation, trying new things, and elevating the art of comedy. This monthly showcase is the place to see tomorrow’s comedy today!

Date: Tuesday, June 22, 2027 at 9:00 AM
Venue: LOOM, 2124 Penn Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, USA
Organizer: intelli global conferences
Description: 8th International Conference On Nursing Education, Midwifery & Healthcare
nurses, researchers, educators, clinicians, academicians, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and industry experts from around the world to London, United Kingdom , on June 22–23, 2027 . This premier international conference provides a global platform to explore the latest advancements in nursing education, clinical practice, healthcare innovation, and patient care through keynote lectures, scientific sessions, poster presentations, workshops, panel discussions, and networking opportunities. The scientific program covers a wide range of topics including Nursing Education, Clinical Nursing, Critical Care, Community Health Nursing, Pediatric Nursing, Women's Health, Mental Health, Geriatric Nursing, Nursing Leadership, Patient Safety, Digital Health, Evidence-Based Practice, Public Health, Advanced Nursing Practice, and Global Healthcare.
For more information: https://nursingeducationconferences.org/

title: Beta Stage (Saturday, June 26, 2027)
text:

Recurs: Monthly, on the last Sat
Venue: Arcade Comedy Theater, 943 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh PA, 15222, USA
Category: comedy
Organizer: Arcade Comedy Theater
Description: Support emerging talent and join us for Beta Stage, a monthly showcase of fresh comedy! Experience the excitement of being a part of the creative process as we provide a platform for producers to present and refine new ideas in front of a live audience. New concepts get the opportunity to be workshopped live, allowing for real-time feedback and audience interaction. This show is a part of Arcade’s incubator series, which is all about experimentation, trying new things, and elevating the art of comedy. This monthly showcase is the place to see tomorrow’s comedy today!
