title: Leadership | The Frick Pittsburgh Museums & Gardens
text:
##### The Café at the Frick Update

# Leadership

#### Amanda Dunyak Gillen, Executive Director

On April 9, 2025, The Frick Pittsburgh named Amanda Dunyak Gillen as the organization's next Executive Director.

Learn More

Amanda has served the museum for more than 20 years, holding various roles spanning the Curatorial and Education departments before becoming head of the Learning department in 2013. In addition to overseeing all adult, student and family programs related to the museum’s diverse collection, Amanda has been responsible for initiatives under the Frick’s Strategic Plan and supported the recent award-winning reinterpretation project at Clayton. In prior years, she was part of the design team for the Frick’s $15 million dollar expansion that resulted in the creation of a new Visitor Center, a renovated Car & Carriage Museum, collections storage, and a new Education Center with facilities to support programming for learners of all ages and needs. Amanda earned a B.A. in History from Allegheny College, where she also received a certificate in Elementary Education, and an M.A. in Public History from Duquesne University.

#### Barry Adams, Director of Human Resources

Barry Adams joined the Frick in June of 2019 as Manager of Human Resources and was made Director in April 2021. He earned his B.S. in Human Resources from Point Park University and has over 25 years of HR experience. Most recently, he retired from the Allegheny County Port Authority where he was Chief Human Resources Officer. His work history includes Westinghouse Electric Corp., Equitable Resources (now EQT), and Schwan’s Home Service.

#### Dawn Reid Brean, Chief Curator & Director of Collections

Dawn joined the Frick as Associate Curator of Decorative Arts in 2015. In her current role, she oversees the care, exhibition, and interpretation of the Frick’s permanent collection and temporary exhibitions. She has played an instrumental role in continuing the Frick’s programming with contemporary artists, including an artist-in-residency with celebrated citizen-artist Vanessa German. A graduate of the College of William and Mary, Dawn earned her M.A. in Museum Studies from the Cooperstown Graduate Program.

#### Kristin Garbarino, Director of Marketing & Communications

As Director of Marketing and Communications since November 2022, Kristin brings fresh, strategic thinking to bear on all aspects of the museum’s marketing and communications, ensuring that the Frick’s website, social media accounts, print materials, advertisements, and campus wayfinding reflect its inclusive goals. Kristin comes to the Frick from Carnegie Mellon University, where she has served since 2018, most recently, as Associate Marketing Director at the Tepper School of Business. Prior to joining the Tepper School of Business, she served as the Director of Digital Marketing & Engagement at the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust.

#### Lisa Gehring, Director of Finance

Lisa Gehring joined the Frick staff in October 2019 as Director of Finance. In this role, she oversees the museum’s $9M operating budget and manages various aspects of the $90M endowment. Lisa brings over 20 years of not-for-profit accounting experience, most recently as the Senior Director of Finance at Manchester Bidwell Corporation. She is a licensed CPA, with a B.S. in Accounting from Grove City College.

#### Robert W. Henninger, Director of Operations

Rob joined the Frick as Director of Operations in October 2022 and manages the museum's maintenance, grounds, and housekeeping teams. Additionally, Rob guides all capital projects across our historic 10-acre, 10-building site. He came to the Frick from Kennywood Park, the National Historic Landmark traditional amusement park founded in 1898, where he has served for 32 years, most recently as Assistant General Manager and Director of Maintenance and Construction. With broad-ranging experience in mentoring effective teams, managing multi-million-dollar capital projects and improvements, and implementing safety initiatives, Rob pairs operations expertise with deep commitment to diplomatic, quality visitor service.

#### Ashley Legg, Director of Enterprise & Visitor Services

Ashley joined the Frick team in 2025 as Director of Enterprise and Visitor Services, in which she oversees Visitor Services, The Café at the Frick, the Frick Museum Store, and Events. Ashley brings over a decade of museum experience to the team, with expertise in Visitor Services operations and management. She strives to create intentionally welcoming and inclusive visitor experiences for all, with the help of talented frontline teams. Ashley holds a bachelor's degree in history from the University of Colorado.

#### Kelsie Paul, Director of Learning & Visitor Experience

Kelsie has more than a decade of museum experience in education and interpretation, sharing her passion for history and the arts with visitors at the Frick since 2017. She currently serves as the Director of Learning and Visitor Experience, overseeing learning department initiatives and supporting the work of a talented staff of educators and guides. In her previous role as Manager of Interpretation and Engagement, Kelsie managed the development and implementation of the Frick’s award-winning new Clayton tour, Gilded Not Golden. She is a graduate of the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign with a degree in History and she earned her Master’s degree in Museum Studies from The George Washington University. Prior to moving to Pittsburgh, Kelsie began her museum career at two presidential sites, President Lincoln’s Cottage and George Washington’s Mount Vernon.

#### Mark Springer, Director of Safety & Security

Mark Springer is a veteran of the United States Navy with over 17 years of experience in law enforcement as a police officer. He has also served as Chief of Police in two communities in Western Pennsylvania. Following his law enforcement career, Mr. Springer has spent the last 20 years in various prominent security leadership roles within the Pittsburgh security market in both Operations and Business Development. He brings extensive experience in contract security services and security technology to the Frick. Additionally, Mark is a licensed private investigator in Allegheny County and has been recognized as a CHS-IV by the American Board for Certification in Homeland Security.

#### Suzanne Wray, Director of Advancement & Engagement

Suzanne joined the Frick as the Director of Advancement & Engagement in March of 2024. With a distinguished career spanning various cultural and educational institutions, Suzanne returns to her Pittsburgh roots from eastern Pennsylvania and New Jersey, where she made significant contributions to organizations such as the New Jersey State Aquarium, Free Library of Philadelphia, and the Philadelphia Orchestra. Most recently, she served as the Director of Development at the Princeton Symphony Orchestra, where she spearheaded successful fundraising campaigns and played a pivotal role in establishing the organization's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) task force. Suzanne began her career in Pittsburgh, serving in development roles at the Pittsburgh Opera and the Bach Choir of Pittsburgh. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Music Performance and Music Education, as well as a Master of Arts Management degree, all from Carnegie Mellon University.

##### The Café at the Frick Update

## Land Acknowledgement

The Frick Pittsburgh occupies ancestral lands of the Haudenosaunee, Lenape, Osage, and Shawnee peoples. As a place of history and nature, the Frick recognizes the cultural importance of land and the role of cultural institutions in the formation of collective memory. Displacement and erasure are not just histories for native peoples. Land acknowledgements, like historic sites themselves, are exercises in preservation and reconciliation, engaged with past, present, and future.

title: New Music Venues Will Liven Up Pittsburgh Scene | Visit Pittsburgh
text:
# 2 New Music Venues Will Soon Liven Up the Pittsburgh Scene

Your guide to making the most of the rest of summer while planning ahead for end-of-year fun.

Pittsburgh’s culture has been shining through in fun and quirky ways this summer. There were pickle-centric cocktails temporarily available at downtown hangouts (the Spritzery pop-up, Space Bar) and themed Pirates games like Yinzerpalooza, featuring giveaways like the coveted Dr. Robby bobblehead doled out to the first 20,000 attendees. If you’re still in the market for a bobblehead, be one of the first 21,000 fans at the game on Tuesday, September 15, to bring home a mini version of hometown hero Roberto Clemente.

Music has filled our fields and amphitheatres all summer long, with the luckiest artists (like Lisa Loeb and O.A.R) receiving perfect-10 weather on the evening they hit the stage. We’ve been especially happy to learn of sweet, unique collaborations this month like one between the Black Keys (who played Stage AE Monday, August 3) and The Peach Truck, which allowed fruit-loving Yinzers to pick up juicy treats for themselves ahead of time. (We discovered that band members have been friends of The Peach Truck for years, so the connection felt natural for everyone involved. They say this partnership celebrates something bigger than peaches or music, and is about “preserving and sharing the traditions that make the South so special.”)

## LOOKING TO AN ARTS-FILLED SEASON AHEAD

Never fear, plenty of concerts are still left in the season, including those that are free. A few other shows topping our radar include: Zac Brown Band: Love & Fear Tour August 13 at PPG Paints Arena with Old Crow Medicine Show, who in June released their new album called Union Made. PPG also welcomes Kacey Musgraves (September 8), Olivia Rodrigo (September 29 and 30) and The Red Stray Clays (October 1). Then there are happenings at Thunderbird, from rising singer/songwriter Solya (September 4) to captivating storyteller/singer/songwriter John Craigie (September 10). Mr. Smalls welcomes Margaret Glaspy (September 18) and Nation of Language (September 21), while Stage AE brings in Sierra Ferrell and Seattle folk/Americana band The Brudi Brothers (September 1) plus Ohio folk talents Caamp (September 25).

As we look ahead, the coming months will see us slowly filling calendars with indoor fun, too — from concerts and lectures to story slams and comedy shows (hello…Golden Girls!). And in very exciting second-half-of-2026 news, there will be several brand-new venues ready to welcome us in in the months to come.

## WELCOMING CITIZENS LIVE AT THE WYLIE

By October, there will be a new, 4,000-capacity venue in town, and there’s much buzz around its opening. Tom Loudermilk, Pittsburgh Market President, Live Nation, says that Citizens Live at The Wylie will fill an important gap in Pittsburgh’s live music ecosystem as the only year-round, indoor venue of its size. “That flexibility will help grow the city’s music scene and attract touring artists who may not previously have had the right place to perform here,” he predicts.

The venue is being touted as an investment in the Lower Hill. Loudermilk says it’s projected to generate $66 million in annual economic impact, create around 350 permanent jobs and support neighborhood residents, businesses and cultural institutions through several long-term community commitments.

There’s been talk of a venue like this for a decade, since Pittsburgh has always had passionate music fans and a vibrant concert scene. Loudermilk believes there’s been a need for a purpose-built, indoor venue of this size. Citizens Live at The Wylie was created to fulfill that while investing in one of the city's most historic neighborhoods.

From the beginning, the vision was to create more than just another concert venue. We wanted to build a destination that attracts world-class artists, creates memorable experiences for fans and honors the rich musical heritage of the Lower Hill District.

Tom Loudermilk

Loudermilk also adds how rewarding it’s been to watch that vision take shape over the past few years.

The venue’s been called a physical homage to an iconic era of Pittsburgh hospitality and nightlife, since the Lower Hill District once played an incredible role in shaping Pittsburgh's musical identity. Some of the greatest jazz musicians in history performed here, and the neighborhood was known for its vibrant scene and sense of community.

“We want guests to feel connected to the history of the neighborhood while experiencing a modern venue that will help write Pittsburgh's next chapter in live entertainment,” Loudermilk says. That history is reflected throughout the building with artwork, historic imagery and references to iconic neighborhood landmarks. And thanks to a partnership with the Carnegie Museum of Art, works from the Charles “Teenie” Harris Archive can also be seen in the venue.

So what to expect as a first-time visitor? “From the moment fans arrive, we want every part of the experience to feel seamless and memorable,” Loudermilk says. Fans can take in a show from the general admission floor, seated balcony, premium suites or in exclusive hospitality spaces. A rooftop lounge offers views of downtown Pittsburgh, while the Vinyl Room is an intimate listening lounge inspired by Japanese high-fidelity listening bars that features a curated record collection, chef-driven fare and creative cocktails.

“Together, these spaces are designed to make a concert feel like a full night out,” Loudermilk says. “At the end of the day, we want people to remember not only the artist they saw, but the experience they had.”

He’s personally impressed by just how much thought went into honoring the neighborhood, which will be visible in nods to the Hill District's musical legacy woven throughout the spaces. Yet all the conveniences and technology expected of a modern entertainment venue will be present too. The premium hospitality spaces have been designed as “destinations,” they say, whether folks gather here pre-show or simply soak in the atmosphere throughout the evening.

A venue of this size can offer great versatility, which is reflected in the opening calendar. On the roster so far, you’ll find artists spanning hip-hop, rock, pop, country, R&B, metal and comedy. Think Wiz Khalifa (October 2), Foster the People (October 4), Chelsea Handler (October 9), Boyz II Men (October 16) and Smokey Robinson (October 23), and that’s only a sampling of what’s already booked.

Loudermilk can’t wait for that first moment when the lights dim and thousands of fans get to experience this venue together. “You can design a building and plan a concert,” he says, “but it's the connection between artists and audiences that brings it to life.”

He adds that that's what Citizens Live at The Wylie is all about — “creating a place where fans can feel close to the music, artists can connect with the crowd and Pittsburgh has a venue that will create unforgettable memories for decades to come.”

## MAKING MUSIC MAGIC AT MIC DROP

On the North Shore, a new nightlife destination called Mic Drop will bring 4,321 square feet in which to enjoy live entertainment, music, craft cocktails and what developers have described as “elevated social experiences.” It’s set to open by the end of the year.

Herky Pollock, president and CEO of Legacy Hospitality Partners, says the idea for this concept has been an evolution. Above all, he and his team strongly believe the North Shore has become the preeminent entertainment district east of the Chicago. “We are seeing more and more customers craving live entertainment,” he says. “We are leaning heavily into this niche and offering different forms of live music.”

Mic Drop will be a fully immersive experience, he promises. “One day you will be a performer, and the next you will be the audience.” It will be a place to play both night and day, and to “let loose in a fun, experiential way.”

Compared to other venues around town, this one will stand out for its mix of offerings, from “bandeoke” and karaoke to dueling pianos and live performances. Everyone can get involved; various forms of participatory entertainment will happen throughout the month.

“We will have day parties so that you can party in the day and be home by 10,” Pollock says. “We will also have parties for late night. There will be something for everyone,”

So what part brings Pollock the most excitement? “Bandeoke,” he says. “You will be the star in your own band. Who wouldn’t want to do that?”

He adds that Mic Drop will be the perfect complement to recently-opened SugarBird, The Plaza at North Shore and the soon-to-be-opened Highball Social Club, as well as their expansion of Shorty’s. As a huge proponent of all things related to this city, Pollock says, “We could not possibly be more bullish on Pittsburgh and the North Shore.”

text:
# Pittsburgh Fall Festivals 2026 Guide

Colorful foliage. Crisp air. Pumpkins. What's not to love about Fall?

As the temperatures start to cool down, fall festival season begins heating up! Explore a pumpkin patch at a scenic farm, celebrate at cultural festivals in the city and more with Pennsylvania's stunning fall colors as a backdrop. Happy Fall!

Halloween fans, we have a list of haunts and ghost tours in Pittsburgh for you, too.

October

November

## September

### Kickoff and Rib Festival

#### September 3-7, 2026 Acrisure Stadium | 100 Art Rooney Avenue, Pittsburgh

Western PA football kicks off right at Acrisure Stadium, home of the Pitt Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers! Enjoy five days of football, amazing ribs, live music, the area's largest cornhole tournament and more at this free fest.

### ReelAbilities Film Festival

#### September 3-13, 2026 Various locations in Pittsburgh

The ReelAbilities Film Festival presents award-winning films through the lens of individuals living with disabilities. In addition to impactful films, the festival also features artwork and special guests to bring the themes of community and shared human experience to the forefront. ReelAbilities is a program of Film Pittsburgh.

### Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival

#### September 4-6, 2026 Market Square/Boulevard of the Allies between Stanwix and Wood Streets

Enjoy a Soulful Taste of the Burgh at this free festival spotlighting Black culinary, butchery, and food businesses. While the fantastic food takes center stage, a small business market, live music, BBQ contest, and cultural activities make this event an all-day affair!

A post shared by Acrisure Stadium (@acrisurestadium)

### Britsburgh

#### September 8-13, 2026 Various locations in Pittsburgh

Bringing a bit of Britain to Pittsburgh, the 2026 Britsburgh Festival is chock-a-block with events from afternoon teas and cask tapping to Shakespeare performances and even a polo match, all designed to bring people together over a shared love of all things British!

### Pittsburgh Irish Festival

#### September 11-13, 2026 Carrie Blast Furnaces | 801 Carrie Furnace Boulevard, Pittsburgh

Guests at this year’s Pittsburgh Irish Festival can expect to see their favorite Irish international, national, and local acts in person at the event’s 34th Annual Celtic Celebration! The line-up features new bands, phenomenal solo performers, well-known favorites, local Irish dance groups, and more on four stages for non-stop fun and enjoyment.

### The Original Pittsburgh Taco Festival

#### September 12, 2026 The Stacks at 3 Crossings | 2875 Railroad Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh's top tacos and food trucks take over the Strip District! Enjoy this community-centered event, which features more than 25 food trucks and vendors, plus live music, an art market, and family fun. This festival is produced with the support of the Pittsburgh Hispanic Development Corporation and Latin American Cultural Union.

A post shared by Pittsburgh Taco Fest (@pghtacofest)

### Phantom Fall Fest

#### Select Dates: September 12 - November 1, 2026 Kennywood | 4800 Kennywood Boulevard, West Mifflin

Experience Kennywood's new Phantom Fall Fest! Visit the park during the day for family-friendly fun, including festive food and a unique Kennywood autumn atmosphere. After dark, the Phantom takes screams to the extreme with seven haunted houses and four scare zones.

### Screenshot: Asian Film Festival

#### September 16 - September 23, 2026 Harris Theater and the University of Pittsburgh | 809 Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh

Harris Theater is hosting an Asian Film Festival, showcasing 12 feature films and 10 short films that highlight Asian culture and experience. Ranging from animated shorts to television episodes to modern movies, the event offers a variety of media fit for whatever you're looking to enjoy.

A post shared by Screenshot: Asia (@screenshotasia)

## Pittsburgh International Jazz Festival

#### September 17 - 20, 2026 The August Wilson African American Cultural Center | 980 Liberty Avenue

Head to the August Wilson African American Cultural Center for our annual International Jazz Festival. This event brings classical jazz as well as modern jazz to the main stages of Pittsburgh and curates an impressive lineup of musicians ready to showcase their musical talent.

### 15th Annual Ukrainian Food Festival

#### September 18-19, 2026 St. Peter & St. Paul Ukrainian Orthodox Church | 220 Mansfield Boulevard, Carnegie

The Parish of Sts. Peter & Paul Ukrainian Orthodox Church will host their annual Ukrainian Food Festival in September this year. Shop traditional Ukrainian baked goods, grab plates of classic dishes, and enter your name to win one of the event's raffle baskets.

### Panda Fest

#### September 18 - 20, 2026 Station Square East Lot Parking | 73 East Carson Street, Pittsburgh

Celebrate Asian culture with 80+ Asian food vendors and over 200 street vendors at the Panda Fest right here in Pittsburgh. Try dishes from China, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, and more, then shop local artisans' goods, from art to clothing to accessories and more.

After shopping, sit in on one of the cultural programs, featuring traditional art, dancing, performances, and more live entertainment. Centering this event is the festival's mascot, pandas! Snap a picture with the many panda posters, inflatables, and themed treats.

A post shared by Panda Fest Pittsburgh (@pandafestpittsburgh)

### Penn Brewery Oktoberfest

#### September 18-20 & 25-27, 2026 Penn Brewery | 800 Vinial Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh's classic Oktoberfest is back at Penn Brewery for 2025! Join us the weekends of September 19-21 and 26-28 at Penn's Northside location for fresh beer, German food, and live oompah music!

### Pittsburgh Chinese Cultural Festival

#### September 19, 2026 Mellon Park | 1047 Shady Avenue, Pittsburgh

Come experience the biggest Chinese community event in Pittsburgh at this free festival. Celebrate Chinese heritage, watch traditional performances, listen to beautiful music and enjoy some delicious food.

### Jump Cut Pittsburgh Noir Film Festival

#### September 19, 2026 The Parkway Theater & Film Lounge | 644 Broadway Ave, Mckees Rocks

Be part of the inaugural Jump Cut Noir Film Festival! 2026 marks the first-ever Noir Film Festival in Pittsburgh, which is scheduled to feature indie films, filmmakers, cocktails, Q&As, workshops, and mingles for those who adore the niche film genre.

### FestPGH

#### September 19, 2026 Highmark Stadium | 510 W Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, Highmark Stadium will resound with the music of bands including the headliner Switchfoot, as well as laughter, games, family fun, service opportunities and worship during the inaugural FestPGH music and arts festival.

A post shared by PGHchineseculturalcenter (@pghchineseculturalcenter)

## South Park Hay Day

### September 19 & 26, 2026

#### 19th: Hartwood Acres Park | 4000 Middle Road, Allison Park 26th: South Park Fairgrounds | 1888 Brownsville Road, South Park Township

Join Allegheny County Parks for a day full of free, family-friendly fall activities. Families can enjoy hay rides, a hay maze, a pumpkin patch trip, a barnyard petting zoo, and more. Food, beverages, and snacks will be available for sale from food trucks and vendors.

## Sharpsburg Summer Jam Music Festival & Bicentennial Drone Show

#### September 19, 2026 Kennedy Park | 1311 N Canal Street, Sharpsburg

Close out the summer with a live performance at the Sharpsburg Summer Jam Music Festival & Bicentennial Drone Show. The event will bring together incredible local performers, taking to the stage throughout the day from 1 pm to 6 pm. Dance to the music and eat from their lineup of food trucks, enjoy family-friendly activities, and drink brews from Sharpsburg's own brewmasters.

### Evans City PumpkinFest

#### September 19 & 20, 2026 Evans City | East Main Street, Evans City

Evans City is ringing in the new season with its fifth annual PumpkinFest. Featuring live music, fall festivities, food trucks, wagon rides, car shows, free games, and more, the festival will take over East Main Street with community fun for all.

### Fall Migration Festival

#### September 20, 2026 Stormy Oaks Nature Conservancy | 120 Forsythe Road, Valencia

Celebrate over two decades of local wildlife education and rehabilitation at Wildbird Recovery’s 15th Annual Fall Migration Festival, an annual fundraiser where supporters of all ages spend time outdoors, enjoy delicious food, and learn about different aspects of our local wildlife.

A post shared by Wildbird Recovery (@wildbirdrecovery)

### Four Chord Music Festival

#### September 25 - 26, 2026 F.N.B. Stadium | 510 W Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

The 2026 lineup at the Four Chord Music Festival is sure to rock, with bands like Knocked Loose, Pierce the Veil, Mayday Parade, and Boys Like Girls. If you're into rock music or just love the music scene, reserve your tickets and get ready for a weekend-long festival of concerts, fun, and local community.

Reserve your tickets for the event on the Four Chords' website.

### 73 Hour Record-Breaking Infinite Cypher - Hip Hop Festival

#### September 25 - 28, 2026 Forest Farms | 441 Grange Hall Road, Tionesta

Feel like breaking a world record? Bring your friends and dance it out at the 73 Hour Infinite Cypher Hip Hop Festival. Looking to break the Guinness World Record for the longest rap marathon event, the Hip Hop Festival will be running for 73 straight hours (that's over 3-days long!).

This is a camping event, so be sure to pack your backpack and have your camping equipment ready to get the most out of the festival.

### Butler Fall Festival

#### September 26, 2026 Downtown Butler, PA | Main Street

The Butler Fall Festival takes place on Main Street in Butler, PA. The event will include a car show, kids activities, artisan and craft vendors, food vendors and music!

### Tropical Forest Panama Festival

#### September 26, 2026 Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens| One Schenley Park, Pittsburgh

Celebrating its Tropical Forest Panama exhibit, the Phipps Conservatory is throwing a festival that will have educational programs and cultural celebrations. Learn more about Panamanian culture, try Latin American food from Pittsburgh's own El Sabor Latin Kitchen, and explore Phipps' latest garden.

A post shared by INFINITE ♾️ CYPHER (@infinitecypher)

### The Pittsburgh Great Race

#### September 26- 27, 2026 Starts at Frick Park at Beechwood Boulevar

Lace up your running shoes and challenge yourself to the annual Great Race right here in Pittsburgh. Compete in the 5K, 10K, or the junior race for any families with track stars in their midst. For every registration, the race donates $1 to the Richard S. Caliguiri Amyloidosis Fund, which supports medical research conducted here in Pittsburgh.

### Pittsburgh Silent Film Festival

#### September 27 - October 4, 2026 Various location in Pittsburgh

Enjoy twelve films from the silent film era screened at eight venues throughout Pittsburgh, all with live musical accompaniment.

## October

### Oktoberfest Pittsburgh

#### October 1-11, 2026 Downtown Pittsburgh

Taking place over 11 days, this year’s event will be held at Fort Duquesne Boulevard, utilizing the westbound roadway from Stanwix Street to 7th Street and incorporating the 6th Street Bridge. This year promises an even better celebration of culture, food, music, and community, so festivalgoers can fully immerse themselves in German-inspired activities for all ages!

### Confluence PumpkinFest

#### October 2-4, 2026 Confluence | Along Routes 281 and 523

Participate in a Fall Foliage celebration during the Confluence PumpkinFest. The festival includes a variety of events like the Pumpkinfest Queen Pageant, a 5K run/walk, an antique and classic auto show, a parade and a largest pumpkin contest.

### Reel Q Film Festival

#### October 2 - 10, 2026 Multiple Locations

The 41st annual Reel Q Film Festival has announced its 2026 dates. A staple of the Pittsburgh film scene, this festival highlights queer filmmakers and stories with their multi-day festival that takes over Carnegie Mellon University in October. See new film premieres, catch local short films, and even get the chance to meet young filmmakers with tickets to the Reel Q festival.

Purchase tickets on the Reel Q official website.

A post shared by Downtown Pittsburgh (@downtownpitt)

### Jack O’Lantern Extravaganza

#### October 2 - November 1, 2026 Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium | 7370 Baker Street, Pittsburgh

Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium will illuminate the city with thousands of artistically carved pumpkins glowing on your night walk through this gourd-geous new display. ZooBoo trick-or-treating will also return during daytime hours, the last two weekends of October.

### Leechburg Annual Fall Festival

#### October 3, 2026 Leechburg Riverfront Park | Kiski Avenue, Leechburg

Head to Leechburg for fall-themed activities, games, local makers, crafters, vendors, fall-inspired food and treats, music, and family-friendly Halloween festivities. The annual fall festival is free for you to attend and brings a day of festival fun to the riverfront park, which offers a great view of the water as a backdrop to the event.

### Mars Applefest

#### October 3, 2026 145 Grand Avenue, Mars

Experience the Mars Applefest with food, fun, shopping, games, crafts, 150+ vendors and entertainment.

### Festival of Combustion

#### October 3, 2026 Carrie Blast Furnace | 801 Carrie Furnace Boulevard, Pittsburgh

This one is sure to be lit fam (is that what the kids say?). The hottest fall festival returns to Carrie Blast Furnaces with hands-on demonstrations, tours of the property, live music, craft beer, and food trucks.

### Fall Apple Fest

#### October 3, 2026 Portersville Steam Show Grounds | 1512 Perry Highway, Portersville

A vintage village, sawmill, cider press, Amish donuts, antique car rally, gas engines, oilfield equipment, farm animals, train rides, steam engines, flea market, crafts, food, kids’ pedal tractor pulling, tractor pulls, and a steam building are some of the features to enjoy.

A post shared by Rivers of Steel (@riversofsteel)

### Pumpkin Festival

#### Weekends in October starting October 3, 2026 Reeger's Farm | 755 Laurel Road, Shelocta

Start a new family tradition at Reeger's Farm! On Saturdays and Sundays in October, they offer hayrides, a pumpkin patch, food trucks, and more.

### Freedom Farms Fall Fest

#### Weekends in October starting October 3, 2026 Freedom Farms | 434 Overbrook Road, Valencia

Any weekend in October, enjoy tons of fall activities like tractor rides, a corn maze, a hay mountain, a petting zoo, pick-your-own flowers, pumpkin carving and decorating, and lots more family-friendly activities.

### Autumnfest

#### October 3-18, 2026 Seven Springs Mountain Resort | 777 Water Wheel Drive, Champion

Treat yourself to a spectacular weekend in the mountains and enjoy the best of Pennsylvania's beautiful fall foliage! Hop on the chairlift for an aerial view of the fiery colors of autumn. Shop from local artisans and crafters, enjoy live music, and take a mini getaway in the mountains during Autumnfest.

### Autumn Serenade Luncheon Cruise

#### October 7, 14, 10 & 17, 2026 Gateway Clipper Fleet at Station Square | 350 West Station Square Drive, Pittsburgh

Enjoy a tasty autumn harvest lunch while taking in the sights of Pittsburgh's fall foliage on a riverboat tour.

### Fort Ligonier Days

#### October 9-11, 2026 Fort Ligonier | Various locations

Fort Ligonier Days is a three-day festival that commemorates the Battle of Fort Ligonier, a key engagement of the French & Indian War. The festival features historic battle reenactments, live music, authentic crafts, delicious food and more.

A post shared by Seven Springs Mountain Resort (@7springspa)

### Houston Pumpkin Festival

#### October 9-11, 2026 124 West Pike Street | Houston, PA

Features family fun for all ages, including over 175 food and craft vendors, music and entertainment, children's games and activities, a parade, and many pumpkin-related contests. Free admission.

### Annual Country Fall Festival

#### October 9-11, 2026 Downtown Zelienople | Various locations

Enjoy two days of musical entertainment, three towers of paranormal ghost walks, pumpkin and costume contests, chainsaw carving, petting zoo, free horse-drawn wagon rides, and historic encampments and demonstrations during the Zelienople Country Fall Festival.

And while you're there, check out the Sleepy Hollow Festival in Historic Harmony! You can even take advantage of a shuttle that runs between the two towns to enjoy everything both festivals have to offer!

### Pittsburgh Dragon Boat Festival

#### October 10, 2026 Pittsburgh Brewing Company | 150 Ferry Street

Head down to the Allegheny River to cheer on riverboat teams as they compete to win the festival's boat race. After the race, swing by some of the vendors and be sure to drop a donation or two with the festival team, as this event supports breast cancer survivors in a one-of-a-kind festival.

### Fall Flower Show

#### Opens October 10, 2026 Phipps Conservatory & Botanical Gardens | 1 Schenley Park, Pittsburgh

With the blockbuster Summer Show, Alice in Wonderland-themed displays are here to stay through the fall! Opening Sat., Oct. 10, Fall Flower Show: Alice’s Adventures in Autumn combines the whimsy of Phipps’ unique take of Lewis Carroll’s story with our stunning chrysanthemums — and a few spooky surprises!

You'll see all your favorite characters from the book among expertly grown chrysanthemums in an endless variety of shapes, colors and sizes. Phipps has been creating chrysanthemum-themed seasonal shows since 1894, making its Fall Flower Show the longest-running in the nation and a Pittsburgh tradition that you can't experience anywhere else!

A post shared by Three Rivers Rowing Association (@3riversrowing)

### Dormont Street & Music Festival

#### October 10, 2026 Patomac Avenue | Dormont

Join us for the Dormont Street and Music Festival, one of the community’s most anticipated events of the year. Taking place rain or shine, this free, all-ages festival offers a full day of live music across three stages featuring 18 bands, along with a wide variety of food, unique arts and crafts, and activities for all. Explore more than 60 vendors, support local businesses and artisans, and enjoy the energy and spirit of the Dormont community with family and friends.

### Pittsburgh Coffee & Chocolate Festival

#### October 17, 2026 Monroeville Convention Center | 209 Mall Boulevard, Monroeville

The Pittsburgh Coffee & Chocolate Festival is a celebration of all things coffee and chocolate-related… and then some! Attendees will sample a variety of coffee roasts and styles, along with a multitude of decadent chocolate-themed sweets from local and surrounding-area businesses.

### Pittsburgh Monster Pumpkins Festival

#### October 17-18, 2026 Pittsburgh Strip District

Join in on the action during the Pittsburgh Monster Pumpkins Festival, featuring a "Costume Caper" 5K run/walk, pumpkin regatta, pumpkin pie eating contest, giant pumpkin sculptures, and, of course, record-breaking giant pumpkins. This year's event is in the Strip District, at 3 Crossings Campus along 28th & 29th Street.

### Fall Fest at the Pittsburgh Playhouse

#### October 23 - November 1, 2026 Pittsburgh Playhouse | 350 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh

The award-winning Pittsburgh Playhouse at Point Park University, a multi-disciplinary arts and entertainment center located in Downtown Pittsburgh, announces the return of Downtown Pittsburgh’s second annual multi-day Fall Fest and the family-friendly hit sensation, Boo’s Halloween House Party. Visitors of all ages can enjoy food & drinks, games, local vendors and arts & crafts onsite of the Pittsburgh Playhouse, with activities on Forbes Avenue during the weekend.

### Trick or Trolley

#### October 24-25, 2026 Pennsylvania Trolley Museum | 1 Electric Way, Washington

Come to the Pennsylvania Trolley Museum to trick-or-treat among the antique streetcars! Visit tables run by local businesses and organizations and collect all kinds of candy and holiday favors. Costumes are encouraged for all ages!

## November

### Three Rivers Film Festival

#### November 4 - 15, 2026 Multiple Locations

Mark your November calendars for the annual Three Rivers Film Festival. If you love indie filmmaking, support the local arts, or simply love a good movie, the Three Rivers Film Festival gives you the opportunity to catch brand-new films from emerging artists. The event also hosts workshops for those looking to sharpen their craft or break into the industry.

Grab your tickets on the Three Rivers Film Festival website.

### Latin American and Caribbean Festival

#### November 7, 2026 Wesley W. Posvar Hall, 1st Floor | 230 South Bouquet Street, Pittsburgh

It's official! The Latin American and Caribbean Festival has become the largest and most significant gathering of Latin American and Latinx communities in Western Pennsylvania! Don't miss out on the event's cultural celebrations, performances, foods, and more!

Yes, our fall calendar is pretty impressive, but it's just the tip of the iceberg for all the incredible events we host in Pittsburgh. Visit our Events page for more festivals, happenings, and offbeat events that take place year-round in the city.

title: Accessibility
text:
## Accessibility

The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust strives to create a welcoming and inclusive arts experience for all. Accessibility services are available to support a wide range of access needs before and during your visit.

Browse the information below to learn more about available services. To request accommodations please call 412-456-6666. Requests that require coordination should be submitted at least two weeks prior to the event whenever possible.

### Guest Service Device Centers

The Benedum Center and Byham Theater have designated spaces to pick up accessibility equipment. The Benedum Guest Services Device Center is located on the house right side of the inner vestibule (between the lobby and the theater). The Byham Theater Guest Services Device Center is up the ramp, past the first set of stairs, and to the right.

Accessible seating is available for purchase online, by phone, or in person. Please indicate your seating needs at the time of purchase to help us accommodate your request.

Curbside wheelchair assistance is available upon arrival.

Our theaters and galleries are located in Pittsburgh’s Cultural District. This downtown setting offers many parking options in lots, garages and on the street. Most parking areas are just blocks from any of our theaters. Patrons are always welcome to drop off and pick up directly in front of the doors of any theater or gallery. For real-time parking information, visit the Park PGH central website.

For patrons desiring to park as close as possible to our theaters, we recommend the Theater Square Garage.

Theater Square Garage

- Close to the Benedum Center and O’Reilly Theater

- Car entrance on 7th St. between Fort Duquesne Blvd. and Penn Ave.

- Pedestrian entrance at 667 Penn Ave.

- 16 accessible spaces

Large print programs are available for most shows at the Benedum and Byham theaters at the Guest Services Device Center.

Braille programs are available for the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series and are produced by the Western Pennsylvania School for Blind Children. Braille programs are also available for other shows by requesting two weeks in advance. Programs can be found at the Guest Services Device Center.

The GalaPro app* is in operation for select PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series performances. GalaPro is free to download and available on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Learn more about the app by clicking here.

#### 2026-2027 PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Season GalaPro Performances

GalaPro will be available for all performances Wednesday through Sunday, with the exception of The Who's Tommy. Patrons requesting captioning for The Who's Tommy should call 412-456-6666 or fill out the online request form, at least 10 days in advance. Fill out the online request form by clicking here.

*Gala Pro service depends on the functionality of your device and a strong Wifi connection.

Audio description is available for Saturday and Sunday matinee performances of the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series*. Audio Description is also available for select performances of other series and by request 14 days in advance. Trained audio describers give live verbal descriptions of actions, costumes, scenery and other visual elements on stage. Audio description begins with show notes 15 to 20 minutes prior to the start of the performance and requires an assistive listening device, available at Guest Services.

VIEW BROADWAY SHOWS

NEW! The Harris Theater now has digital captioning and audio description captioning equipment. Visit TrustArts.org/Film to find digital screenings that offer these features.

If you would like to request ASL or audio description services click here.

Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) amplify and clarify sound by cutting down or eliminating ambient noise. The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust maintains a number of different ALDs. Speak with the guest services representative at your venue to select the best one for you.

ALDs are available at all venues for all performances on a first-come, first-served basis.

Sennheiser MobileConnect is an assistive- and personal listening solution that streams live audio content via WiFi to any iOS or Android phone in the room. This app can only connect to Bluetooth enabled hearing devices. MobileConnect is currently available at Benedum Center performances. For information about connecting to the service, please follow the instructions linked below.

Sennheiser MobileConnect Information Guide (PDF)

Captioning available upon request. Requests need to be made two weeks in advance of the performance.

The Harris Theater now has digital captioning and audio description captioning equipment. Visit TrustArts.org/Film to find digital screenings that offer these features.

Sign language interpretation is scheduled for select PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh performances throughout the season, and can also be arranged upon request. Requests for sign language interpreters must be received at least two weeks prior to the event, and are subject to the availability of an interpreter. If you would like to request ASL or audio description services click here.

Sensory inclusive performances are events for patrons of all ages and abilities. They are designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities and others who would like to enjoy a performance in a relaxed environment. These performances are modified to create a friendly, supportive environment, without editing or altering the content of the show. Adjustments for these performances may include:

- Access to resource materials such as social stories, picture schedules, character sheets and videos

- Reduction of jarring and dramatic sound and lighting effects

- Raised house lights

- Specially trained ushers and volunteers

- Fidgets available for use throughout the performance

- Designated quiet and activity spaces

Sensory Guides

Sensory Guides are available for patrons attending Broadway performances Friday through Sunday. These short guides outline sound cues, lighting shifts, sudden effects, and unexpected key production moments to help guests prepare for sensory changes throughout the show. You can pick one up at the Benedum Guest Services Device Center when you arrive. To request the information prior to Friday after opening night please email ksmith@trustarts.org with the subject "Sensory Guide".

Individuals with sensory sensibilities or invisible disabilities shouldn’t miss out on special events, experiences, and dreams. Our partner,Kulture City, creates sensory accessibility and inclusion for all. Kulture City sensory bags are designed to help sensory needs in both adults and children. Filled with items that can help lessen sensory overload and also engage individuals, the bag items are easily cleaned and sterilized for multiple uses.

Find social stories for the Byham Theater here and for the Benedum Center here.

An adult changing table is now available at the Benedum Center. It can be found in the Benedum Center's accessible restroom in the Clark Extension.

Service dogs and miniature horses are welcome in all of the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust’s theaters and facilities.

The Benedum Center and Byham Theater have lactation rooms that can be used throughout performances. The Benedum lactation room is located upstairs on the Promenade level near the Patron Bar. The Byham lactation room is located in Guest Services at the top of the Ramp Lobby on the main level.

title: Photography Policies | The Frick Pittsburgh Museums & Gardens
text:
##### The Café at the Frick Update

# Photography Policies

### Visitor Photography Policy

We encourage visitors to capture and share photography for non-commercial, personal use under the following guidelines:

- Posed photography sessions (family portraits, engagement photos, senior portraits, and similar shoots) are permitted on The Frick Pittsburgh's grounds and in the Greenhouse, as long as they are not blocking or impeding visitors and the organization's events

- Posed photography sessions are not permitted within The Frick Art Museum or the Car and Carriage Museum

- Non-posed personal photography is permitted in the permanent collection galleries of the Frick Art Museum and Car and Carriage Museum

- Non-posed personal photography is allowed in special exhibition galleries at the Frick Art Museum unless otherwise noted

- All personal photography is permitted in the Greenhouse and on the grounds of The Frick Pittsburgh

- Photography of any kind is prohibited inside the historic mansion, Clayton

- Only photography with hand-held devices (phones, hand-held cameras, tablets) is permitted

- No flash is permitted

- Visitors must maintain an 18" distance from any art or artifacts

- Use of tripods or other stationary camera equipment is not permitted at any time

- Selfie sticks are permitted outside on the grounds, but not indoors

- Aerial photography is prohibited

- Photographs and videography cannot be published, sold, reproduced, or otherwise commercially exploited in any manner whatsoever

- The Frick Pittsburgh is not responsible for any uses of visitor photography that infringe upon third-party copyrights or other rights

- Visitors taking photos are asked to please be courteous to other visitors by not blocking their view or impeding their movement

- Visitors to The Frick Pittsburgh may be photographed, videotaped, or otherwise recorded. Visitors grant The Frick Pittsburgh permission to use photographs and/or audiovisual recordings.

### Commercial & Business Photography Policy

We require photographers and videographers shooting for commercial or business use to obtain a permit in advance. Permits start at $150 with set-ups including one camera person using hand-held equipment only. Use of static equipment, such as tripods, requires an additional fee for staff time.

Requests for permits must be submitted at least 10 business days in advance and are subject to staff availability. Permits are non-refundable. In the case of inclement weather, permits can be rescheduled depending upon availability.

Please email media@thefrickpittsburgh.org with your desired date and time, crew size, and camera set up to request a permit.

title: Pittsburgh Autumn Visitor's Guide | Visit Pittsburgh
text:
# 2026 Visitor's Guide to Autumn in Pittsburgh

Forge your perfect fall getaway in Pittsburgh with beautiful colors and cozy vibes all season long.

With a mix of indoor and outdoor options, those looking to relax and explore will enjoy Pittsburgh any time of the year. Check out some ideas to plan your perfect autumn trip below:

## For the Family

From outdoor family fun to engaging family-friendly museums, kids of all ages will love Pittsburgh in the fall.

- Interactive Fun for Small Children

Embrace adventure at the Children's Museum of Pittsburgh with interactive exhibits like the kindness gallery, makeshop®, garage and studio. For the older youth, be sure to visit MuseumLab for cutting-edge experiences in art, tech, metalworking and learning.

- Step into a Safari at the Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium

Take in the chilled air during a trip to the zoo. The Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium is tucked away into the sprawling green hills of Highland Park, and feels like it's in its own world even within the city limits. With so many animals to see - think elephants, giraffes, red pandas, and more - your time at the zoo will be a full-day adventure. Visit in October for ZooBoo and the Jack O'Lantern Extravaganza!

- Take a Ride at Kennywood

Just because summer's over doesn't mean it's too late to go to the amusement park. Kennywood's rides will have your kids screaming for another go-around all season long. Perfect for thrill seekers and the little ones alike, this not-so-hidden gem outside of the city is a must-visit for families. Be on the lookout for Phantom Fall Fest, which takes over the park every October.

## For the Foodie

While Pittsburgh is the destination for foodies all year, fall in Pittsburgh is a special treat. Between seasonal events and spaces that feature diverse options, foodies will obsess over the impressive possibilities.

- Pumpkin spice is back in full swing

Pumpkin spice takes over the world every fall, but Pittsburgh handles the craze in a way you've never seen. Our local coffee shops and restaurants go all-in when it comes to the fan favorite flavor. Don't know where to start? We've highlighted the top spots to get your fall-flavored drinks this season.

- Take in a cool day at a coffee shop

Is there much better than sipping on a delicious cup of coffee? Luckily, Pittsburgh is home to plenty of cozy coffee shops that you can escape, for the days where the weather isn't quite as warm as you want it to be.

## For the Outdoor Enthusiast

Pittsburgh's unique environment makes for interesting outdoor fall activities for adventurers of any age and skill level. Whether you're looking for casual sightseeing or intense seasonal fun, there's a perfect fit for you.

- Embark on a Fall Adventure

Fall is the perfect time to take in a brisk hike, and luckily Pittsburgh is teaming with trails fit for the most novice or seasoned hiker. Whether you're going along one of our rivers or venturing out into the surrounding hills and mountains, you'll find a hike that you'll remember heading into the winter months.

- Book a Bike Ride

Pittsburgh is a bike-friendly city, with plenty of trails and bike lanes just waiting for you to explore. Either BYOB - bring your own bike - or rent one from POGOH before hitting the pedal to the metal.

- Walk Through Incredible Gardens

Explore the beauty and wonder of nature at Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens. The stunning Victorian glasshouse showcases seasonal flower shows, special exhibits and a nationally recognized orchid collection, making Phipps a must-see Pittsburgh attraction no matter the time of year.

## For the Sports Fan

Cheer on the Pittsburgh Pirates at PNC Park

If you're looking for an outdoor sports adventure, the Pittsburgh Pirates season is in full swing - pun intended - during the fall months. Catch a fireworks night or a promotional giveaway while enjoying one of the best views from an MLB stadium.

Swing Your Terrible Towel at a Pittsburgh Steelers Game at Acrisure Stadium

Alexa, play Renegade! The fall means that the Pittsburgh Steelers are back in action at Acrisure Stadium in the North Shore. Grab your Terrible Towel and cheer on the Black and Gold all season long.

Watch NHL Legends Take the Ice with the Pittsburgh Penguins at PPG Paints Arena

Fall is a unique time in Pittsburgh, because all of our major sports teams are playing at the same time! The Pittsburgh Penguins begin their season at PPG Paints Arena in October, and now's the perfect time to see NHL legends - both seasoned and in the making - take the ice right before your eyes.

Celebrate Pittsburgh Sports

Celebrate the accomplishments of sports in the region with a visit to the Franco Harris Sports Museum at the Heinz History Center, hidden gem The Roberto Clemente Museum in Lawrenceville and the Steelers Hall of Honor at Acrisure Stadium.

## For the Arts Admirer

- Enjoy Broadway in Pittsburgh

For the theater enthusiast, don't miss the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh series, presented by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. The 2026 season features Disney's the Lion King.

- Connect with Art at CMOA

The visual arts are also thriving this winter with various works of arts and new exhibits on display at the Carnegie Museum of Art. And for 2026, the 59th Carnegie International invites you to take part in its vision with this rendition's theme, "If the word we."

- "POP" into The Andy Warhol Museum

Explore seven floors of Warhol’s art, films and life at The Andy Warhol Museum, one of the most comprehensive single-artist museums in the world. In addition to experiencing Warhol’s work, you can create your own at The Factory, an underground studio with activities designed to bring out your inner artist. Sit for a screen test or try your hand at silkscreen or watercolors.

- Explore Pittsburgh's Gilded Age at The Frick

The Frick Pittsburgh is a collection of art and history museums located in Pittsburgh’s East End neighborhood. The museum includes a collection of 19th century European art, ever-changing exhibitions and a collection of historic cars and carriages.

- Release Your Creativity at the Mattress Factory

Hailed as the best facility for installation art in the United States, this contemporary art museum is an experimental lab featuring site-specific installations created by artists in residence from around the globe. Each exhibition takes you into another world that evokes a unique perspective.

For even more fall activities in Pittsburgh, check out our Outdoor Fun blog.

title: Things to Do in Pittsburgh This Autumn - Visit Pittsburgh | Visit Pittsburgh
text:
# Autumn in Pittsburgh

Forge Your Fall Adventure in the Steel City

There just aren’t words to describe the beauty of fall in Pittsburgh. The season begins with summer temperatures cooling down, then the picturesque fall foliage slowly spreads throughout the rolling hills that make up the city’s landscape. The hues of the skyline will spark your imagination from the second you step foot into the city, setting the scene with the perfect backdrop for exploring our three rivers, rolling hills, and walkable neighborhoods.

What to Pack

Autumn Weather

Things to Do

## What to Pack

The good news is that fall in Pittsburgh is full of colorful trees and warm temperatures, perfect for outdoor exploration. However, because our rivers and evening breezes can bring the cold after dark, dressing smart is the key to a great trip.

When packing, there are a few things you should be sure to grab:

- A Jacket is a Must: Despite the warm temperature sticking around, the air will definitely cool down. A jacket, even if it's light, is essential to a trip to Pittsburgh in the autumn.

- Comfortable Walking Shoes: Pittsburgh is incredibly walkable, from the North Shore trail to historic neighborhood business districts. Bring durable sneakers or supportive sandals.

- Sun Protection is Essential: Don't forget your sunglasses, sunscreen, and a rimmed hat or baseball cap to stay comfortable during afternoon ballgames or river cruises.

- Break Out Those Sweaters: We know you've been itching to bundle up in your favorite sweater, so take this as your sign to finally break it out for the season. And while you're at it, get those fuzzy socks out too.

## Autumn Weather Overview

Pittsburgh autumns are the perfect mix of warm and cool, which means no matter your weather preference, you'll find it here during your trip.

- September: Average High 78°F (25°C) | Average Low 57°F (14°C)

- October: Average High 65°F (18°C) | Average Low 45°F (7°C)

- November: Average High 53°F (12°C) | Average Low 35°F (2°C)

## Things to Do

Whether you want to maximize your time in the waning sunshine or want to cozy up away from the brisk air, a Pittsburgh summer offers the perfect mix of experiences.

- Enjoy the Views from the Inclines: Take a ride on the Duquesne Incline for breathtaking panoramic views of the city. Hop on a bike and ride the 24+ miles of riverfront trails and beyond – the Great Allegheny Passage is a must in the fall for biking enthusiasts. Or, book a walking tour with ‘Burgh, Bits & Bites Food Tour or Walk the Burgh Tours to discover more reasons why Pittsburgh is so special.

- Explore Pittsburgh's Spooky Scene: Plan a visit before Halloween and explore the spookier side of Pittsburgh with haunted attractions like Zombies of the Corn and Hundred Acres Manor. Families can partake in the Halloween fun, too, with ZooBoo at Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium.

- Take in the Best of Pittsburgh's Sports: Fall also is a fantastic time of year for sports fans. Join Steelers Nation at Acrisure Stadium for a one-of-a-kind experience cheering on the Pittsburgh Steelers. From fall festivals to food festivals, Three Rivers Beer Week, world-class theater experiences and more, visitors are sure to find an entertainment option that fits their interest.

text:
## Safety, Security, and Health

SECURITY SCREENING PROHIBITED ITEMS BAG POLICY GUEST CODE OF CONDUCT HEALTH CONSIDERATIONS

The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust wants you to feel at home in the Cultural District and in our venues. That means we are committed to making sure you—our guests, staff, volunteers, and artists—feel safe both physically and psychologically when you’re in our spaces.

### Security Screening

Even before you take your seats, you can feel safe knowing that all guests are subject to a physical screening and inspection prior to entry. These security practices are in effect at the Benedum Center, Byham Theater, and O'Reilly Theater.

The screening process is enhanced by a security technology called EVOLV systems. Included in this system are contactless screening machines which allow guests to seamlessly walk through with their bags, coats, and permissible items.

By presenting your ticket and entering our venue, you consent to such screenings. Refusal of screening may result in denied entry. These protection measures have been put in place to ensure that each performance or experience is occurring in the safest environment possible for our guests.

### Prohibited Items

The following is a list of outside items which are prohibited inside of venues owned and/or operated by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust.

- Weapons of any kind or facsimiles of weapons, including firearms, pellet guns, stun guns, martial arts weapons, pepper spray, pocket/utility knives or cutting instruments

- Illegal drugs or substances

- Flammable liquids

- Fireworks, pyrotechnics, flares or incendiary devices

- Glass, metal, or plastic containers of any kind including cans, bottles and flasks (plastic or metal water bottles are permissible but must be empty upon venue entry-unless for child or infant use)

- Outside food or beverages including alcohol

- Oversized bags that exceed 16” x 16” x 8”

- Interchangeable/detachable camera lens (No professional photography-unless authorized)

- Audio/visual recording devices.

- 2 way radios

- Laser pointers

- Laptops (tablets are permitted)

- Beach balls, projectiles, balloons, permanent markers, spray paint

- Drones

- Flashlights

- Signs, flags, banners

- Selfie sticks

- Guests without shoes or shirts

- Masks which cover the full face (Halloween in nature or full face covering)

- Face paints

- Optical illusions

- Jewelry that could be used as a weapon including chains and studded bracelets

- Pets, other than service animals

- Segways, skateboards, rollerblades, hoverboards, bicycles, helmets, any type of portable seat, other than those approved and required for accessibility

- Noisemakers, bullhorns, or air horns

- Unapproved pamphlets, handouts, advertisements

- Unattended items left outside venue doors will be discarded to ensure guest safety.

This list is not all-inclusive and may change or be updated at any time without notice. Additional restrictions may apply.

### Bag Policy

A guest to a Pittsburgh Cultural Trust venue or event may enter with one bag that is no larger than 16” x 16” x 8”. The definition of a bag includes, but is not limited to, purses, tote bags, duffel bags, suitcases, knapsacks, backpacks, packages, cartons, paper sacks, briefcases, portfolio cases, binocular cases, camera equipment cases, and any other type of device or vessel used for carrying or concealing items.

Bags are subject to search and theatergoers may be requested to open their jackets prior to entering. Guests with prohibited items may return them to their vehicles. Unattended items left outside the facility doors will be discarded to ensure patron safety.

### Guest Code of Conduct

The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust is committed to providing you a safe, comfortable, and enjoyable entertainment experience. Guests have a right to expect an environment where everyone can and will:

- Be treated in a consistent, professional, and courteous manner by all theater personnel.

- Feel comfortable reporting inappropriate behavior to an usher, house manager, or security officer.

- Comply with requests from venue staff and security regarding facility operations and emergency response procedures.

- Sit only in their ticketed seats and show their tickets when requested.

- Consume alcoholic beverages in a responsible manner and in compliance with law.

- Not interfere with the event or performers in any way.

- Not smoke or use tobacco-related products anywhere inside the theater at any time.

- Not attempt to re-enter the venue without a ticket or appropriate credential.

- Wear a shirt, shoes, and lower garments at all times.

Guests who engage in fighting, throwing objects, using foul/abusive language or gestures, attempting to enter restricted areas, or any other behavior deemed detrimental to the experience of other guests will be immediately ejected from the venue and may be subject to police action for these violations.

Your ticket is a revocable license exclusively valid for the event listed on the ticket and is subject to the full terms and conditions found here and terms located on ticket backs. Theater management reserves the right to revoke this license without refund for non-compliance with any Pittsburgh Cultural Trust terms and policies. Theater staff may intervene where necessary to ensure that the above expectations are met, and guests are encouraged to report any inappropriate behavior to the nearest usher, security guard, or staff member. Guests who choose not to adhere to these provisions may be subject to ejection without refund and, to the extent their conduct constitutes a violation of law, may be subject to arrest and prosecution.

### Health Considerations

We want to make sure our venues not only keep you safe, but that you also leave healthy. If you feel sick, we ask that you prioritize your health and the health of others by staying home and contacting the box office for ticketing options.

#### Masks

Masks are not required while attending indoor events taking place at Pittsburgh Cultural Trust theaters and facilities. Our facilities are mask-friendly environments, and we ask that all guests be respectful of one another's choices.

#### Additional Layers of Defense

The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust has implemented additional layers of defense in our venues.

‘Gold Standard’ in Cleaning

The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust practices the same gold standard of cleaning that is used by the Global Biorisk Advisory Council (GBAC) Star Facility Accreditation for stringent protocols for cleaning, disinfection, and infectious disease prevention in our facilities.

Restrooms are extensively disinfected prior to every event, including toilets, handles, sinks, countertops, soap dispensers, faucets, and adult and baby-changing stations. We have also installed new, touchless fixtures in many of our facilities.

High-touch areas throughout our venues, including door handles, handrails, countertops, and elevator buttons are being cleaned prior to all events.

We provide an ample supply of hand sanitizer and seat wipes. The Pittsburgh Cultural Trust has proactively placed hand sanitizers at every front door and throughout each of our venues. Seat wipe dispensers have also been added at central locations in every venue.

Clean Air in Our Venues

We have improved overall air quality, expanded the use of high-efficiency filters, and added new HVAC technologies. The Trust has reviewed and improved air quality in all our venues. We have also equipped all HVAC systems with upgraded, Merv-16 rated filters, which have been identified to be much more effective in trapping microscopic particles, including COVID-19.

title: Pittsburgh Fall Date Ideas | #LovePGH | Visit Pittsburgh
text:
# Pittsburgh Fall Date Ideas

Cozy up with that special someone on these fall-themed date nights

It's finally fall! If you're in need of a spooky-, pumpkin spice- or harvest-themed date night idea, Pittsburgh has you covered. There's only so much time before the fall festivities turn into reindeer games, so make the most out of fall with these Pittsburgh date night ideas.

## Hayrides and Pumpkin Patches

Pittsburgh is surrounded with farmers markets, and there's no better time to visit than the fall. Head to Trax Farms, Soergels Orchards, or Shenots (to name a few) for the ultimate fall-time date. Pittsburgh offers plenty of festivals to carve a pumpkin, get “lost” in a corn maze or go on a hayride. If you are not sure which one to check out, take a look at our Fall Festivals Guide

## Hold Me (For Dear Life) Date Night

Not for the weak-hearted, Pittsburgh is a top spot for haunts and the go-to escape for haunted house enthusiasts. This date night will test your relationship (and survival skills) as you enter Pittsburgh's ultimate haunted houses, including Hundred Acres Manor bringing the screams, or Zombies of the Corn which arms you with a paintball gun and lets you fight back against the zombie horde.

Related: Halloween Events in Pittsburgh

## Phantom Fall Fest

If you're an adventure-seeker or just a kid at heart, you'll want to explore Phantom Fall Fest at Kennywood. Come early and ride the Phantom's Revenge and other scream-inducing rides, then stick around after dark for phantoms stalking you through haunted houses and scare zones! This is the perfect date night complete with white-knuckle roller coasters, devilishly good food and spine-tingling fun.

## For Horror Film Lovers

Pittsburgh's horror heritage is unmatched. It's where zombie movies first made their mark, bursting out of their graves and onto the scene with Pittsburgh filmmaker George Romero's Night of the Living Dead and Dawn of the Dead. Plan a zombie-infested date night seeking out filming locations before binging these made in PGH flicks.

If you can't get enough of scary movies, then head straight to Bierport bottle shop and Rowhouse cinema for date night. Bierport's taproom is now open seven days a week, so find a new favorite (bonus for going local), then bring it to the other side of the building into Rowhouse for your horror film of choice.

## DIY Fall Candles

There's nothing like filling your house with the sweet smell of fall. At Mix Candle Co. in Pittsburgh, you can create your very own custom candle. You start out by selecting your scents with the expert candle makers and then proceed with making the candle. This is a great way to start your date night and, while your candle is drying, you can pop over to any of the surrounding Lawrenceville bars or restaurants.

## Makers Activities

If the candle and paint date night ideas are passé for you, don't worry. Pittsburgh has tons of ways to stay active and create together so you go home with something truly one-of-a-kind.

Take a jewelry making or wood class with Contemporary Craft, create your own custom scents with Galimard, forge a ring with the expert blacksmiths at The Barefoot Forge or sign up for a Make-It-Now workshop at Pittsburgh Glass Center to take home coasters, cups and even blown glass pumpkins!

Perfume & Cologne creation at Galimard Pittsburgh

Credit |
Jordan Beckham, courtesy of House of Handsome

## It's Showtime

Sure, summer is great, but fall is when the Cultural District really comes to life! Our fall 2026 season of shows includes the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh production of Disney's The Lion King, plus productions from the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra, Pittsburgh Opera, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre, Liberty Magic and more! Add in national touring comedians and immersive theatre options, and this is the best time of the year to attend a show.

## FYF: Find Your Festival

I'll be honest, I plan my date night activities right from our fall festivals page. Seemingly every weekend there is something new and different to enjoy including pumpkin festivals, Pittsburgh Irish Festival, fall foliage cruises and so much more.

Find somewhere to eat and a place to grab a drink afterward, and planning your date night takes less than five minutes for a guaranteed good time.

## Get Thrifty

The joy of discovery is the reason why thrifting has become such a trendy thing to do in Pittsburgh. You never know what store might hold the perfect piece that's been missing from your wardrobe. Luckily, we developed our guide to thrifting in the city to help you find the best bargains, upcycled clothing and eco-friendly creative surplus and supplies stores.

B-Sides Vintage in Millvale

## Picnic in the Park

Another reason I love Pittsburgh so much: You don't need to spend a ton on tickets to have a good time. Slow things down and enjoy a date night at one of the parks surrounding the city, taking plenty of stops for photos and a blanket for snuggling. Better yet, fill a picnic basket with some of your favorite Pittsburgh foods to snack on as you watch the leaves change.

## Take a Walk Around Phipps

Phipps Botanical Gardens is a great spot to walk around with your special someone and see the beautiful fall flowers. Nothing in Pittsburgh adjusts to the seasons like Phipps!

Opening Oct. 10, 2026, see their Fall Flower Show: Alice’s Adventures in Autumn, which combines the whimsy of Phipps’ unique take of Lewis Caroll’s story with our stunning chrysanthemums — and a few spooky surprises! You'll see all your favorite characters from the book amongst expertly grown chrysanthemums in endless shapes, colors and sizes. Phipps has been creating chrysanthemum-themed seasonal shows since 1894, making its Fall Flower Show the longest running in the nation and a Pittsburgh tradition that you can't experience anywhere else!

## Pittsburgh Sports, Here We Go

For our couples out there that like watching sports, a Pittsburgh Penguins hockey game is a great option. Pens games are exciting, vibrant and capture the magic of a fall day or night in Downtown. College Students: don’t forget to use Student Rush!

If hockey isn't your game, the end of the Pirates and Riverhounds seasons collides with the beginning of Steelers and Pitt Panthers football seasons during fall, making the hardest part of date night getting tickets to these high-energy events.

## Make a Fall Beer Tour

Pittsburgh's breweries and beer-centric are celebrated throughout the year, but fall is always an ideal time to discover that new brewery together. Pittsburgh neighborhoods have great breweries around every corner, and fall means it's time for festive new releases like pumpkin stouts, brown ales, porters, stouts and much more along with Oktoberfest celebrations at seemingly every location.

Follow our beer map and plan your route for fall flavors.

## Dinner and a View

Pittsburgh has so many great restaurants and places to take in a nice view, why not combine that into one night? Go to a North Shore restaurant and walk the river trail, or from Market Square to the Point, or even from Station Square up the incline to Mt Washington! There are endless combinations to try around the city.

title: Apple Picking & Pumpkin Patches | Visit Pittsburgh
text:
# Apple Picking & Pumpkin Patches: Day Trips from Pittsburgh for Fall Fun

The air is getting crispy and the sunsets are getting earlier. Are you ready for fall?

In my opinion, it's never too early to break out your sweaters and start planning your trips to the pumpkin patch or apple orchard. Pittsburgh has plenty of options for those fall outings you've been looking forward to all year, including several locations that will act as your one-stop-shop for all your picking pleasures.

## Pumpkin Patches

## Trax Farms

Location: Finleyville, PA

Hours: Monday-Sunday, 10am-6pm

Fall Fest: Every Saturday & Sunday Sept. 20 - Oct. 26, 2025, 10am - 5pm

My personal bias is that Trax is the best pumpkin patch in the Pittsburgh area. I'm not saying that as a knock on all the others; I just love all that Trax has to offer. From wine tastings to hayrides, dreamy fall and winter candles to fresh produce and flowers, Trax really has it all. I think of all the pumpkin patches I've been to in the Pittsburgh area, Trax has the best selection of pumpkins even as Halloween draws closer; I've gone as close as four days before Halloween and still got several pumpkins that I carved. Their pumpkin piles also make for great photo spots (as pictured).

And when the air gets a little too chilly, the inside of Trax features must-sees and must-buys for the whole family. I recommend going early so you can check out the thrift/antique store on the second floor. I also recommend leaving with a giant bag of kettlecorn popcorn to tie you over for the fall months.

Trax also has a Fall Fest filled with activities for the whole family, which you can learn more about here.

## Soergel Orchards

Location: Wexford, PA

Hours: Monday-Sunday, 9am-6pm

Harvest Schedule: Flower fields open Saturday, Sept. 14, 2025. Pick your own apples and pumpkins Sept-Oct. Pick your own blueberries July-Aug.

At Soergels, you get the best of both worlds in the form of a pumpkin patch and an apple orchard. I've personally never been apple picking there, so I can't vouch for the experience, but I can tell you that I make sure to get some sour apples every time I go to get pumpkins.

Walking through Soergels on a crisp fall day feels like walking through an autumn wonderland. There are shops designed like little cottages, farm animals you can interact with, a market where you can get fresh produce, and a greenhouse for all of your flowery needs. The pumpkin patch is up on a hill, with a gorgeous view of the landscape that makes for a great backdrop for your photos. It's been to go early in the season to get your best pick of the patch, and I cannot stress enough: wear comfortable shoes! I made the mistake of wearing heeled boots once, and I'll never do it again.

## Bedner's Farm Market

Location: Upper St. Clair, PA

Hours: Market open daily 10am-5pm

Bedner's isn't a pumpkin patch per se, but they've got plenty of pumpkins to go around. Conveniently located on Bower Hill Road at the edge of Upper St. Clair and Bridgeville with ample parking, Bedner's offers always fresh in-season selections from their farm in Mercer, PA, just over an hour north of Pittsburgh. If you're looking for more opportunities to pick your own produce, Bedner's Farm and Greenhouse in Cecil Township offers pick-your-own tomatoes, peppers, herbs, and more.

## Apple Orchards

## Shenot Farm

Location: Wexford, PA

Hours: Market open daily 10am-6pm

Harvest Schedule: Pumpkin patch open late Sept. - late Oct. Apple harvest from early July - early Nov.

The Shenot family has been in the Pittsburgh area for seven generations, and the community they've built showcases the quality of their product. Complete with pick your own apples and flowers, apple cider with a recipe honed over several generations, and homemade fudge with 20 flavors made with lots of love, Shenot Farm is a must-stop for your fall itinerary. The business also prides itself on its sustainability, and the taste and quality of its products makes that evident.

A post shared by Shenot Farm (@shenotfarm)

## Triple B Farms

Location: Monongahela, PA

Hours: Monday-Sunday, 9am-5pm

Harvest Schedule: Apples available for picking Sept. - Oct., pumpkins available for picking late Sept. - late Oct.

An apple orchard, pumpkin patch, and sunflower field all in one. Triple B Farms is your home for fresh, local, sustainably grown, delicious produce, and wholesome family fun. I cannot recommend going on a Saturday enough, because Saturdays at Triple B are Artisan Bread Saturdays, and the artisan breads are mouthwatering.

Click here for Triple B's harvest schedule.

A post shared by Triple B Farms Official (@triple_b_farms)

## Simmons Farms

Location: McMurray, PA

Hours: Monday-Thursday, 9am-6pm; Friday-Sunday, 9am-5pm

Harvest Schedule: Apples available for picking late summer/fall, pumpkins available for picking fall

Apples, pumpkins, strawberries (and more), oh my! At Simmons, you can take your pick at your picks, from produce to flowers and a few things in between. Apple and flower picking are open daily, with no reservations needed for the flowers. Simmons also hosts a variety of events throughout the year, including candle making and wildflower picking.

Click here for Simmons' full pick-your-own schedule.

A post shared by Simmons Farm (@simmonsfarminc)
